items.title: [E6-T16] CI assertions: tenant tables RLS and no dbt full rebuild
items.body:
## Summary
Add CI checks that every tenant-schema table has RLS and that dbt never full-rebuilds a tenant table.

## Description
Plan E6 done-when: 'dbt gold models pass the CI assertion that every tenant-schema table has RLS enabled, forced, with policies, and no dbt run does a full-table rebuild of a tenant table; only `fa_tenant_lookup` is `SECURITY DEFINER`.' Build a test script (pytest against compose Postgres after migrate + dbt run): (1) every table with a `tenant_id` column in the app schemas has `relrowsecurity` and `relforcerowsecurity` true and >=1 policy; (2) `pg_proc` has exactly one SECURITY DEFINER function, `fa_tenant_lookup` (extend, do not duplicate, E1-T17 if it exists); (3) a static check over dbt models that rejects `materialized='table'` for any model reading a tenant table, and a runtime check that no `DROP TABLE`/`CREATE TABLE AS` for tenant tables appears in the dbt run's executed SQL log. Gate in CI.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a new table with tenant_id and no RLS, when the assertion runs, then it fails naming the table (negative test)
- [ ] Given a dbt model with `materialized='table'` over `chunks`, when the check runs, then it fails (negative test)
- [ ] Given the clean repo, when run, then the only SECURITY DEFINER function is `fa_tenant_lookup`
- [ ] The checks are wired into the CI workflow and block merge

## Architecture
- deep-dive/05-data-model-and-storage.md#5.2
- deep-dive/04-components-and-responsibilities.md#4.8

items.title: The simulated orchestrator
items.body:
## Parent

#220

## What to build

A scheduled Lambda that plays Airflow and dbt: `daily_orders`, `hourly_events` and `weekly_finance`. Its models run real SQL in the demo workgroup, with the dbt-athena comment carrying `node_id`, `invocation_id`, `team`, `tenant_id` and `dag_run_id`. It writes OpenLineage events and dbt artifacts to the Inbox, templated from `fixtures/reference-workload/` (ADR 0030, spec 09).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Under Stubber and a fixed seed, every event and artifact passes the existing readers
- [ ] Every query's first line is a Trusted Query Comment
- [ ] Ingesting its output links each Query Execution to its Model Execution and on to the DAG run
- [ ] Runs start between :10 and :40 past the hour; some tasks fail and retry
- [ ] Its role may start queries only on the demo workgroup
- [ ] Tooling ticket: full loop (TDD, mutation checks, both reviewers)

## Documentation

None beyond the public-demo page.

items.title: [E6-T19] BigQuery isolation, byte-cap and time-travel acceptance test
items.body:
## Summary
Prove tenant views isolate rows, queries are capped and every dataset keeps 48 h max time travel.

## Description
Plan E6 done-when: 'BigQuery tables are day-partitioned, clustered by `tenant_id`, with `maximum_bytes_billed` set; a tenant's authorized view returns only that tenant's rows.' Round 4 (ADR-029 amended, R4-D18 V2): add the time-travel assertion. Add a test that provisions two tenants' views from E6-T17, inserts rows for both and checks (1) tenant A's view never returns B's rows including via `SELECT *`, filters on B's id and a join on the base dataset (denied for tenant A's principal), (2) a query exceeding `BQ_MAX_BYTES_BILLED` is rejected with `bytesBilledLimitExceeded`, (3) table metadata partitioning and clustering, (4) EVERY dataset in the project, including one created by a dbt run (E6-T18), reports `max_time_travel_hours = 48` from `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA_OPTIONS`. Runs in CI against the emulator where it can, and as a gated job against a real test project for authorized views and item (4); the test docs record which.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tenant A principal selecting from tenant A's view returns 0 rows with tenant_id != A; querying the base table directly is denied.
- [ ] A query estimated above `BQ_MAX_BYTES_BILLED` fails with `bytesBilledLimitExceeded`.
- [ ] Given a dataset created by `dbt run` in the test project, when the options are read, then `max_time_travel_hours` is 48 for it and for every other dataset; a dataset at 168 h makes the test fail (test_every_dataset_48h).

items.title: [E6] ETL and data engineering
items.body:
## Summary
ETL and data engineering (phase 2: Product). Scope, ADRs and exit criteria are in the plan section below.

## Plan
- **Goal.** A replayable, idempotent pipeline from raw documents to tenant-scoped, redacted, embedded chunks and analytics.
- **Scope.**
  - Bronze (GCS by sha256); silver (Docling, Presidio, structure-aware chunking with Voyage token counts, Pandera, rejects; Parquet partitioned tenant / dt); contextual headers (Haiku batch, flag); suitability-rule extraction and validation; embed-indexer publishes (chunk identity is the unique 8-column key of deep-dive 05-1 §5.10 including `valid_from`, `parser_version` and `embed_model`; `(tenant_id, chunk_hash, embed_model)` is a non-unique reuse index) and bumps `corpus_version` last.
  - Dagster assets / partitions run daemon-less as Cloud Run jobs from Scheduler, with Postgres run storage (`dagster` database, `fa_dagster`); `dagster dev` locally. Tenant stages run as worker consumers; PUBLIC (EDGAR 497K) runs all stages in-process in `etl-public` and publishes only analytics events. Synthetic per-tenant corpus.
  - dbt gold as `fa_dbt` (`security_invoker` views or incremental models, never full rebuilds); `dbt-bigquery` marts; BigQuery sink with per-tenant authorized views (primary) and row access policies (second layer).
  - ACL change as metadata UPDATE (applier from E5).
- **Arch sections.** deep-dive/04-components-and-responsibilities.md#4.7 to #4.11, deep-dive/04-1-key-flows.md#4.14 (flow 2), deep-dive/05-data-model-and-storage.md#5.2, deep-dive/05-1-rls-indexes-versioning-and-deletion.md#5.8; ADR-014, ADR-016.
- **Dependencies.** E5.
- **Spikes first.** Docling on the 497K HTML and inline-XBRL tables (chunk sizes measured with Voyage `count_tokens`).
- **Done when.**
  - Re-running the same partition re-embeds zero unchanged chunks (count asserted); an ACL change updates metadata with zero embed calls.
  - Every Pandera failure appears in `ingest_rejects`; no raw document text exists outside GCS bronze (scan test of `documents`, `chunks`, events, BigQuery).
  - `suitability_rules` is populated and validated for the synthetic corpus; `lookup_suitability_rule` returns rows on a real DB.
  - dbt gold models pass the CI assertion that every tenant-schema table has RLS enabled, forced, with policies, and no dbt run does a full-table rebuild of a tenant table; only `fa_tenant_lookup` is `SECURITY DEFINER`.
  - The PUBLIC corpus is written only by `fa_etl_public` (test: a worker attempt is denied by policy and a PUBLIC event on a pipeline topic is sent to `dlq.v1`).
  - BigQuery tables are day-partitioned, clustered by `tenant_id`, with `maximum_bytes_billed` set; a tenant's authorized view returns only that tenant's rows.
  - Fixes G-07, G-39, G-62.

- **Round 4 changes (2026-11-02).**
  - Silver path is `silver/tenant_id=/doc_id=/version=` (was tenant / dt), so erasure deletes by prefix and a parser bump re-parses; chunk identity includes `valid_from` and `parser_version` (ADR-014 amended, ADR-027). Supersedes the "partitioned tenant / dt" wording and the "re-running the same partition re-embeds zero unchanged chunks" bullet: replay after a parser bump re-parses, and unchanged chunk hashes extend `valid_to` with no embed call.
  - Atomic publish: the indexer is the only writer of `chunks`; it embeds outside any transaction, then one transaction per document: advisory lock first, tombstone check, `contract_passed AND scan_passed`, insert or extend chunks, version `active`, cache purge, `processed_events`, `corpus_version` row last (ADR-028, R4-D5; one transaction per document). Every sink (`bq-sink`, silver, contextualizer, indexer) guards with the E5 ledger helper; the silver worker checks before and after writing Parquet.
  - Ingest scan stage in the silver worker: parse-time sanitiser (script and style, comments, hidden or off-screen text, zero-width and bidi characters), deterministic pattern list, then quarantine (`status=quarantined`, bytes under `quarantine/`, never silver or chunks). Model Armor document screening is added by E11 (ADR-036).
  - Quality: Pandera with `PANDERA_VALIDATION_DEPTH=SCHEMA_AND_DATA`; dbt `contract: enforced` on gold tables; Dagster blocking checks are advisory only (the atomic gate is the control; cross-run behaviour UNVERIFIED, tested here); BigQuery `max_time_travel_hours=48` on every dataset including dbt-created ones (idempotent repo-managed DDL plus an assertion); OpenLineage dropped (ADR-014 amended, ADR-034).
  - Validation (2026-11-07, ADR-039): BigQuery time travel is set by the project default `default_max_time_travel_hours = 48` (dbt sets no dataset options), with the per-dataset setting as an assertion (ADR-029 amended). Chunk identity and embedding generations follow ADR-035 as amended (R4-D19 M1).
  - Contextual headers are an ablation arm, default OFF; the baseline B0 is the free structural prefix (title plus section path) written by the chunker (ADR-016 amended). Presidio runs English only.
  - Real connectors move to E11; `source_observations` is E11's table.
  - Added to Done when: #1 with a test double that commits a tombstone immediately before the sink write (N interleavings: zero rows or objects; E12 repeats it with the real worker); #5 on synthetic poison (malformed HTML and PDF, a zip-bomb-like size, injection payloads: none indexed, all in quarantine or the DLQ, consumers continue); #8 (replay a fixture corpus twice after a parser bump: the hash equals a single run, zero resurrection); a planted bad row fails Pandera; the BigQuery `max_time_travel_hours` assertion.

## Architecture
- deep-dive/04-components-and-responsibilities.md#4.7 to #4.11
- deep-dive/04-1-key-flows.md#4.14 (flow 2)
- deep-dive/05-data-model-and-storage.md#5.2
- deep-dive/05-1-rls-indexes-versioning-and-deletion.md#5.8
- ADR-014
- ADR-016

## Tickets
- [ ] E6-T1 Spike: Docling on EDGAR 497K HTML and inline XBRL
- [ ] E6-T2 Scaffold the ETL package and daemon-less Dagster
- [ ] E6-T3 Synthetic per-tenant corpus generator
- [ ] E6-T4 Bronze asset: GCS by sha256, register documents, publish
- [ ] E6-T5 Silver transform: Docling parse, Presidio scrub, chunking
- [ ] E6-T6 Pandera validation, ingest_rejects and versioned silver Parquet
- [ ] E6-T7 silver worker role: consume bronze, emit silver, guard writes
- [ ] E6-T8 contextualizer: Haiku headers (default off), guarded sink
- [ ] E6-T9 Suitability-rule extraction, validation and lookup
- [ ] E6-T10 indexer: atomic per-document publish and lock order
- [ ] E6-T11 Replay, parser-bump and ACL-change tests with zero embed calls
- [ ] E6-T12 Dagster partitions and the etl job entrypoint
- [ ] E6-T13 etl-public: in-process EDGAR 497K pipeline as fa_etl_public
- [ ] E6-T14 Raw-text scan test across documents, chunks, events, BigQuery
- [ ] E6-T15 dbt project and Postgres gold models as fa_dbt
- [ ] E6-T16 CI assertions: tenant tables RLS and no dbt full rebuild
- [ ] E6-T17 BigQuery dataset: partitioned tables, views, 48 h time travel
- [ ] E6-T18 dbt-bigquery marts and the ingest_events feed
- [ ] E6-T19 BigQuery isolation, byte-cap and time-travel acceptance test
- [ ] E6-T20 Ingest scan stage and quarantine in the silver worker

- [ ] E6-T22 voyage-context-4 contextualized chunk embeddings as an eval-only generation

items.title: [E6-T17] BigQuery dataset: partitioned tables, views, 48 h time travel
items.body:
## Summary
Create fa_analytics tables with partitioning, tenant clustering, authorized views, row policies and the project-default 48 h max time travel.

## Description
Arch (4.11, 5.8): dataset `fa_analytics`, tables `chat_audit`, `chat_usage`, `eval_events`, `gateway_audit`, `acl_changes`, `ingest_events`; 'day-partitioned, clustered by `tenant_id`; per-tenant authorized views (primary isolation) plus row access policies (second layer); `maximum_bytes_billed` on every query'. DDL as code in the repo (`etl/bq/schema.py` or `bigquery/` SQL, applied by an idempotent `jobs`-callable command) with BQ_DATASET and BQ_MAX_BYTES_BILLED; partition by `DATE(event_time)` with `require_partition_filter`; cluster by `tenant_id`; `ensure_tenant_view(tenant_id)` in a separate views dataset authorized on the base dataset; a row access policy per tenant; all query helpers pass `maximum_bytes_billed`. Subject-bearing tables (`chat_audit`, `chat_usage`, `eval_events`, `acl_changes`) have a `pseudonym_id` column and no text columns; no table holds FCA content or answer text (ADR-013 amended, ADR-026).

Round 4 (ADR-029 amended 2026-11-07, R4-D18 V2, ADR-039): BigQuery time travel is set by the PROJECT default: the DDL command runs `ALTER PROJECT ... SET OPTIONS (default_max_time_travel_hours = 48)` for the dataset region (idempotent), so every new dataset, including dbt-created ones, inherits it; dbt-bigquery sets NO dataset options (not documented). The per-dataset `max_time_travel_hours = 48` is kept only as a CHECK: the same command reads `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA_OPTIONS` for every dataset in the project and exits non-zero if any value differs. Out of scope: the bq-sink writer (E5-T14), onboarding hook wiring.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given the applied DDL, when table metadata is read, then each of the 6 tables has `time_partitioning.type=DAY` and `clustering_fields[0]=='tenant_id'`; no column named answer, excerpt, question or text exists in any table (test).
- [ ] Given the DDL command run on a project whose default is unset, when finished, then the project default is 48 h and a dataset created afterwards (by a plain CREATE SCHEMA) reads `max_time_travel_hours = 48` (test_project_default_time_travel_48h; gated job on a real test project, since an emulator may not model it).
- [ ] Given a dataset whose time travel is 168 h, when the check runs, then it exits non-zero naming the dataset (negative control).
- [ ] Given rows for tenants A and B, when a query runs through tenant A's authorized view, then only tenant A rows return; a query without `maximum_bytes_billed` is rejected by the wrapper; running the DDL twice is a no-op.

items.title: [E1-T8] RLS v2 policies and grants for content tables
items.body:
## Summary
documents, chunks, suitability_rules and ingest_rejects have the own-or-PUBLIC read policies, own-tenant-only write policies, column grants and the fa_etl_public-only PUBLIC write.

## Description
Add an Alembic revision implementing overview 5.4 and the 5.3 grants for the content tables. `<PUBLIC>` is the `PUBLIC_TENANT_ID` uuid literal substituted by the migration; `fa_eval` policies use the `EVAL_TENANT_ID` literal. Policies call `current_setting('app.x')` without `missing_ok`, so an unset setting raises (fail closed).

Policies (policy text for `chunks` is the arch text; `documents` and `suitability_rules` are identical in shape, `suitability_rules` uses `min_tier_required`):
- `*_select_app TO fa_app FOR SELECT`: `(tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::uuid OR tenant_id = '<PUBLIC>'::uuid) AND tier_required <= current_setting('app.tier')::int AND jurisdiction = ANY (string_to_array(current_setting('app.jurisdictions'), ','))`.
- `*_select_pipe TO fa_worker, fa_etl, fa_etl_public, fa_dbt FOR SELECT`: own tenant only.
- `*_ins_tenant`, `*_upd_tenant`, `*_del_tenant TO fa_worker`: own tenant and `tenant_id <> '<PUBLIC>'` (USING and WITH CHECK on UPDATE). `fa_etl` gets INSERT and UPDATE on `documents` with the same own non-PUBLIC clause, and SELECT on `chunks`.
- `*_all_public TO fa_etl_public FOR ALL`: USING and WITH CHECK `tenant_id = '<PUBLIC>'::uuid`.
- `fa_eval`: the `fa_app` policies with the tenant literal of the `eval` tenant plus PUBLIC reads.
- `ingest_rejects`: tenant match for the roles holding grants, no PUBLIC clause.
`fa_app` has no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE policy or grant on `chunks`, `documents`, `suitability_rules` ("document ACL changes and deletes are applied by the `acl-applier` worker (ADR-022)").

Grants per 5.3: `fa_app` SELECT only; `fa_worker` on `chunks` SELECT, INSERT, DELETE and UPDATE (`tier_required`, `jurisdiction`) only, on `documents` SELECT, INSERT, DELETE and UPDATE (`tier_required`, `jurisdiction`, `status`, `parser_version`), on `suitability_rules` SELECT, INSERT, DELETE, on `ingest_rejects` SELECT, INSERT; `fa_etl` SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE (`status`, `parser_version`, `bronze_uri`) on `documents` and SELECT on `chunks`; `fa_etl_public` write on the content tables; `fa_dbt` SELECT; `fa_eval` the `fa_app` grants. Never `GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES` (partitions get no grants).

Out of scope: tenants/advisors (E1-T9), other tables (E1-T10), the full leak matrix (E1-T19, E1-T20).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a principal for tenant A (tier 2, jurisdictions US), when `fa_app` selects from `chunks` after `set_config(..., true)`, then it sees tenant A and PUBLIC rows only, never tenant B rows, never rows with `tier_required = 3`, never rows with `jurisdiction = 'EU'` (`tests/db/test_rls_content.py`, parametrised over `chunks`, `documents`, `suitability_rules`).
- [ ] Given `fa_app`, when it runs INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on `chunks`, `documents` or `suitability_rules`, then each fails with permission denied (no grant).
- [ ] Given `fa_worker` bound to tenant A, when it inserts a chunk with `tenant_id` = B, or with `tenant_id` = PUBLIC, then each raises a row-level-security violation; and when it updates `documents.title`, then it fails with permission denied (column grant).
- [ ] Given `fa_etl_public`, when it inserts a chunk into the PUBLIC tenant, then it succeeds; when it inserts into tenant A, then it raises a row-level-security violation.
- [ ] Given `fa_eval` with `app.tenant_id` set to tenant A, when it selects from `documents`, then it sees only `EVAL_TENANT_ID` and PUBLIC rows.
- [ ] Given no `app.tenant_id` set in the transaction, when `fa_app` selects from `chunks`, then it raises `unrecognized configuration parameter` (fail closed) and returns no rows.

## Architecture

- overview.md#5.3
- decisions.md#adr-002
- decisions.md#adr-004

## Depends on
None

## Size
M

items.title: Remove or secure unwired code paths and add kill switches for procedures and async jobs
items.body:
## Summary
Code that is registered or present but not wired, and would be unsafe if used:
- `McpStdioRunner.cs:25-46` / `McpProtocolHandler.cs:382-410`: caller-chosen `servicePrincipalId` and tenant become the principal, no authentication.
- `GovernedTableCacheExecutionService.cs:172-185`: hard-coded `tenant_id`, string-built filter literals, no virtual/mandatory filters, no transport gate.
- `TableCacheAdminEndpoints.cs:15-18`: never mapped; `RequireAuthorization("AdminPolicy")` names a non-existent policy; handlers have no role/tenant checks.
- dbt file helpers (`DbtMetadataIngestionService.cs:253-285`, `DbtExposurePublisher.cs:67-107`, `DbtContractValidator.cs:146`): prefix denylists, arbitrary-path writes; no callers. `DbtExposurePublisher.cs:36-58` builds YAML by concatenation and writes consumer SIDs.
- `TableStreamEndpoints.cs:164-171`: visibility/admin bypass via `User.IsInRole("admin")` only on bulk/stream.

Also: procedures and async jobs are mapped unconditionally (`GatewayApplicationBuilderExtensions.cs:289-292`); add `Enabled` flags tied to the matching kill switches.

## Proposal
Delete the unused paths (or rebuild on the governed readers with containment checks); unify visibility/admin helpers; add the flags.

---
Found in a read-only security review of `main` at `f081a9d6` (2026-11-04). Line numbers are approximate; verify before fixing.

items.title: [E1-T5] Migration: content tables with LIST-partitioned chunks
items.body:
## Summary
documents, chunks (LIST by tenant), suitability_rules and ingest_rejects exist in the target shape with composite FKs, raw_content dropped, and the PUBLIC and DEFAULT partitions.

## Description
Add an Alembic revision (0002 or later; baseline 0001 is immutable) as `fa_owner` that replaces the MVP content tables with the target shape of deep-dive/05-data-model-and-storage.md §5.2 and 5.5. The MVP `documents.raw_content` column is dropped (G-03: "No `raw_content` column"). The service has never been deployed, so the revision drops and recreates the MVP content tables without a data migration.

Tables, all `FORCE` + `ENABLE` RLS at creation, all with `tenant_id uuid NOT NULL`:
- `documents (tenant_id, id)`: columns per 5.2 (`title, doc_type, jurisdiction, tier_required CHECK 1..4, regulatory_ref, last_reviewed_at, product_category, risk_level, source CHECK in (edgar, synthetic), source_uri, bronze_uri, bronze_sha256, parser_version, status CHECK in (active, superseded, deleted), created_at`); unique `(tenant_id, bronze_sha256)`; index `(tenant_id, doc_type, jurisdiction)`.
- `chunks (tenant_id, id)` `PARTITION BY LIST (tenant_id)`; columns per 5.2 including `embedding halfvec(1024)` and `tsv tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(context_header,'') || ' ' || content)) STORED`; composite FKs `(tenant_id, document_id)` to documents and `(tenant_id, parent_id)` self; identity unique `(tenant_id, document_id, provision_path, chunk_index, chunk_hash, valid_from, parser_version, embed_model)` (round 4, below). Indexes declared on the parent so each partition gets its own: HNSW on `embedding halfvec_cosine_ops` `m=16, ef_construction=64` partial `WHERE kind = 'child'`; GIN on `tsv`; btree `(tenant_id, document_id)`, `(tenant_id, parent_id)`, `(tenant_id, tier_required, jurisdiction)`.
- `suitability_rules (tenant_id, id)`: per 5.2, composite FK `(tenant_id, source_document_id)`, `client_risk_profile` CHECK 3 values (use the values already in the MVP schema).
- `ingest_rejects (tenant_id, id)`: per 5.2.
Partitions: one for the PUBLIC tenant (`chunks_public`) and a DEFAULT partition (`chunks_default`); rows in DEFAULT are a bug. Write a reusable function `src/db/partitions.create_chunks_partition(conn, tenant_id)` (partition name from the uuid, no `GRANT`) that E1-T11 reuses. The partitions are created without any grants.

If E1-T2's ADR changed the partition design, follow the ADR.

Out of scope: policies and grants (E1-T8), tenant partitions (E1-T11), changing the retrieval code that reads these tables (E3).

Round 4 (ADR-027, ADR-035, R4-D3, R4-D19 M1; deep-dive/05-1 section 5.10): (1) `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS btree_gist` first, as `fa_owner`. Availability on Cloud SQL PostgreSQL 16 is UNVERIFIED: the migration fails with a clear message if the extension cannot be created, and the PR records the check on a Cloud SQL instance (or marks it open for E10). (2) `chunks` also carries `provision_path`, `chunk_index`, `kind`, `valid_from date NOT NULL`, `parser_version`, `embed_model`, `valid_range daterange NOT NULL`, `system_range tstzrange NOT NULL`, `is_current boolean GENERATED ALWAYS AS (upper_inf(valid_range)) STORED`, with CHECK `valid_from = lower(valid_range)`. The identity above is UNIQUE (it includes `embed_model`, so generations coexist); the old `(tenant_id, chunk_hash, embed_model)` becomes a plain, non-unique index used to reuse vectors. (3) `create_chunks_partition(conn, tenant_id)` also executes, for the leaf it creates (the PUBLIC partition migration does the same for `chunks_public`), `ALTER TABLE chunks_<tenant> ADD CONSTRAINT chunks_<tenant>_no_overlap EXCLUDE USING gist (tenant_id WITH =, document_id WITH =, provision_path WITH =, chunk_index WITH =, kind WITH =, embed_model WITH =, valid_range WITH &&) WHERE (upper_inf(system_range))`. PostgreSQL 16 cannot declare an exclusion constraint on a partitioned parent, hence per leaf. The composite FKs to `document_versions` and the `documents` column changes of section 5.2 belong to E11-T4/E11-T5 (that epic owns `document_versions`); not here.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given `alembic upgrade head` on an empty database, then `tests/db/test_schema_content.py` passes: `chunks` has `relkind='p'` and `partstrat='l'`, partitions `chunks_public` and `chunks_default` exist, and `documents` has no column named `raw_content`.
- [ ] Given a chunk row whose `(tenant_id, document_id)` points to a document of another tenant, when inserted as `fa_owner`, then it raises a ForeignKeyViolation (composite FK; test).
- [ ] Given `create_chunks_partition(conn, <uuid>)` is called, then a partition bound to that uuid exists and `has_table_privilege` for `fa_app`, `fa_worker`, `fa_etl`, `fa_etl_public` and `fa_dbt` on it is false for every privilege (test).
- [ ] Given two rows with the same full 8-column identity, then the second insert raises a UniqueViolation; given text A (valid 2020-01-01 to 2021-01-01), text B, then text A again with `valid_from` 2022-01-01, the three rows insert with disjoint ranges and no violation (A-B-A test `tests/db/test_chunk_identity.py::test_aba_is_three_rows`).
- [ ] Given the PUBLIC partition, then `pg_indexes` shows an HNSW index with `halfvec_cosine_ops`, `m='16'`, `ef_construction='64'` and predicate `kind = 'child'`, a GIN index on `tsv`, and a NON-unique index on `(tenant_id, chunk_hash, embed_model)` (`test_public_partition_indexes`).
- [ ] Given two current rows with the same `(tenant_id, document_id, provision_path, chunk_index, kind, embed_model)` and overlapping `valid_range`, when inserted into a leaf created by `create_chunks_partition`, then Postgres raises an exclusion violation (SQLSTATE 23P01); the same overlap with `system_range` closed (not `upper_inf`) is accepted; the same overlap with a different `embed_model` is accepted (`test_exclude_per_leaf`).

## Architecture
- deep-dive/05-data-model-and-storage.md#5.2

items.title: [v2 Bug] Spark snapshots leak numbered helper columns for list unique keys
items.body:
### Current Behavior

The dbt v2 Spark snapshot materialization retains numbered `dbt_unique_key_N` staging helpers in both `missing_columns` and `source_columns` when `unique_key` is a list, including a one-item list such as `[id]`.

Confirmed in the source at `43edeffa8bcab72506ce79477762f886ad8be515` and with isolated execution of its Jinja helper-generation and column-filter expressions. Spark excludes `dbt_unique_key`/`DBT_UNIQUE_KEY` but not numbered variants. The shared and Databricks materializations already exclude numbered helpers.

This allows internal helpers into `create_columns` on the second snapshot run. Once present in the target, the staging query's `select *, ... as dbt_unique_key_1` can produce duplicate helper columns on a subsequent run. This is the same source-level defect as dbt-labs/dbt-adapters#2101, with a separate bundled implementation in dbt v2.

### Expected Behavior

Internal snapshot key helpers should remain staging-only. Scalar, one-item-list and composite keys should all exclude their helpers from target schema evolution and merge column lists while retaining ordinary source columns.

### Steps To Reproduce

Minimal live reproduction to validate on Spark/Delta (not executed against a live warehouse for this report):

1. Use a Spark target and create a source table with `id`, `status`, and `updated_at` columns and one unique row.
2. Configure a snapshot with `file_format: delta`, `unique_key: [id]`, `strategy: check`, and `check_cols: [status]`, selecting these source columns explicitly.
3. Run `dbt snapshot` once to create the target.
4. Change `status` for the row and run `dbt snapshot` again. Inspect the target schema for an unexpected `dbt_unique_key_1` column.
5. Change the row again and run a third time. Check for duplicate/ambiguous numbered helper columns in the staging query.

The timestamp strategy and multi-column keys use the same affected column-filter path.

### Relevant log output / verified evidence

No live Spark error log is claimed. Isolated execution of the existing expressions gives:

| Key | Helpers surviving Spark's missing/source filters |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | none |
| `[id]` | `dbt_unique_key_1` |
| `[id, tenant_id]` | `dbt_unique_key_1`, `dbt_unique_key_2` |

### Environment

- Reviewed dbt v2 `main` source at `43edeffa8bcab72506ce79477762f886ad8be515`.
- Source inspection and isolated Jinja checks on macOS ARM.
- No installed dbt v2 release or live Spark/Delta execution is asserted by this report.
- Adapter: Spark (`type: spark`), not the separate Databricks materialization.

### Additional Context

This is an inherited adapter defect, not a claimed regression exclusive to v2. Searches of existing issues/PRs for Spark snapshots, numbered helpers and unique keys, plus inspection of the open PR list, found no matching fix. #16462 concerns Spark driver/type handling; #16084 concerns Iceberg configuration and does not fix this filtering path.

- Affected code: https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt/blob/43edeffa8bcab72506ce79477762f886ad8be515/crates/dbt-loader/src/dbt_macro_assets/dbt-spark/macros/materializations/snapshot.sql#L153-L167
- Helper generation: https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt/blob/43edeffa8bcab72506ce79477762f886ad8be515/crates/dbt-loader/src/dbt_macro_assets/dbt-adapters/macros/materializations/snapshots/helpers.sql#L319-L328
- Separate dbt 1.x adapter fix: https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-adapters/pull/2208

items.title: [E1-T19] L0 leak matrix part 1: cross-tenant reads, writes, FK probes
items.body:
## Summary
A pytest leak-matrix harness proves cross-tenant read, insert, update, delete into PUBLIC, FK existence probes and fail-closed on every table, and reports leaks = 0.

## Description
Build the L0 leak matrix (deep-dive/05-1-rls-indexes-versioning-and-deletion.md §5.4: "The write split and the PUBLIC rule are tested by the L0 leak matrix"; 8.5 leak-path controls). `tests/leak/` with a harness: seed tenants A, B and PUBLIC (plus advisors with different tiers and roles) through `fa_owner`; helper `as_role(role, principal_settings)` opening a connection as that role's login and running statements inside a transaction with `set_config(..., true)`. A result collector counts a *leak* whenever a forbidden statement succeeds or returns a foreign row; the suite fails if `leaks != 0` and prints `LEAKS=<n>` in the output.

Matrix cases in this ticket, over every tenant table (parametrised from `pg_class` so a new table without a case fails):
1. Cross-tenant read: for each role holding SELECT (`fa_app`, `fa_worker`, `fa_etl`, `fa_dbt`, `fa_eval`) bound to tenant A, selecting from each table returns no tenant B row.
2. Cross-tenant insert: for each role holding INSERT, inserting a row with tenant B's `tenant_id` while bound to A raises a row-level-security violation or permission denied.
3. Update and delete into PUBLIC: `fa_worker`, `fa_etl`, `fa_app` (where granted) cannot INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE rows with the PUBLIC `tenant_id`; only `fa_etl_public` can, and only for PUBLIC.
4. FK existence probes: as tenant A, inserting `chunks`, `conversations`, `escalations`, `acl_change_requests` rows referencing ids of tenant B's `documents` / `advisors` fails with a foreign-key violation whose message is the same as for a nonexistent id (no oracle) or a permission error; cross-tenant composite pairs `(A, id_of_B)` fail.
5. Fail-closed: with `app.tenant_id` unset (new transaction on a fresh connection), every SELECT on a tenant table by a policy-bound role raises an error and returns zero rows.

Out of scope: direct partition access, self-escalation, pooled reuse, EXPLAIN pruning and CI gate wiring (E1-T20).

Round 4 (ADR-039 M6, ADR-002 D13a): the matrix stays parametrised from `pg_class`, so tables added by later epics (`document_versions`, `source_registry`, `deletion_requests`, `pseudonym_map`, ...) enter it automatically and need a case. Case 3 is extended: `fa_etl_public` has NO INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on any firm tenant's table (including `deletion_requests`); the FCA purge is a pull model, so it writes only the PUBLIC `source_purges` rows. Tables not yet created by their epic are skipped by the parametrisation and covered when that epic's migration lands.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given the matrix runs against the migrated schema, then `pytest tests/leak -k 'read or insert or public or fk or failclosed'` passes and its output contains `LEAKS=0`.
- [ ] Given a deliberately weakened policy in a negative test (e.g. `chunks_select_pipe` USING (true) in a scratch database), then the matrix reports `LEAKS` greater than 0 and the test asserting detection passes.
- [ ] Given a new table is added to the schema without a matrix case, then `tests/leak/test_coverage.py` fails (table list from `pg_class` must equal the set of tables covered).
- [ ] Given case 4 for a nonexistent id and for an id of tenant B, then the error class and SQLSTATE are identical for both (no existence oracle) or both permission denied.
- [ ] Given case 3, then `fa_etl_public` inserting into tenant A raises a row-level-security violation (the only PUBLIC writer cannot write tenants).
- [ ] Given every tenant table present in the schema, when `fa_etl_public` bound to PUBLIC attempts INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE of a row carrying a firm tenant's `tenant_id`, then each raises a row-level-security violation or permission denied, and the output still contains `LEAKS=0` (`tests/leak/test_public_writer.py::test_fa_etl_public_writes_no_firm_table`).

## Architecture
- deep-dive/05-1-rls-indexes-versioning-and-deletion.md#5.4
- deep-dive/05-1-rls-indexes-versioning-and-deletion.md#5.13

items.title: Dynamic config() parameters from macro return values cause dbt1501 errors

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: A defect: dbt behaves incorrectly versus expected/reference behavior.

labels.name: status:needs-repro
labels.description: Cannot proceed until the reporter provides a reproduction

labels.name: area:engine
labels.description: dbt engine: CLI, task graph, run-time orchestration.

items.body:
## Environment

- **dbt Fusion version**: v2.0.0-preview.154
- **OS**: macOS (Darwin 24.6.0)
- **dbt-core version**: 1.9.x (BigQuery adapter)
- **Project scale**: 282 tenants × ~25 model templates = ~6,500 tenant models, 156k+ auto-generated sources

## Problem

When parsing a multi-tenant dbt project, Fusion reports **6,502 `dbt1501` errors**:

```
dbt1501: Failed to render SQL invalid operation: config requires all arguments to be defined
```

The root cause is that Fusion's static Jinja analysis cannot resolve `config()` arguments that come from **macro return values** (dicts). dbt-core handles this correctly because it evaluates macros before validating `config()` arguments.

## Reproduction

### 1. Helper macro — extracts tenant info from `model.fqn` at parse time

```sql
{% macro macro_get_dir_tenant_info() %}
    {%- set fqn = model.fqn -%}
    {%- if fqn | length > 1 and fqn[1] == "tenant" -%}
        {%- set dir_name = fqn[3] -%}
        {%- set tenant_suffix = dir_name | replace("tenant_", "") -%}
        {%- set tenant_id = "'" ~ tenant_suffix | replace("_", "-") ~ "'" -%}
        {%- set alias_name = model_name | replace("_" ~ tenant_suffix, "") -%}
        {{ return({
            "found": true,
            "dir_name": dir_name,
            "alias_name": alias_name,
            "suffix": tenant_suffix,
            "id": tenant_id
        }) }}
    {%- endif -%}
{% endmacro %}
```

### 2. Model macro — receives dict and passes values to `config()`

```sql
{% macro dim_drawing_by_tenant(tenant_info, materialized="table") %}
    {{ config(
        materialized=materialized,
        dataset=tenant_info.dir_name,
        alias=tenant_info.alias_name,
        tags=[tenant_info.dir_name, tenant_info.alias_name],
    ) }}
    
    -- ... SQL body ...
{% endmacro %}
```

### 3. Model file (one per tenant, ~6,500 files)

```sql
-- models/tenant/prod/tenant_xxxxxxxx_.../dim_drawing_xxxxxxxx_....sql
{% set tenant_info = macro_get_dir_tenant_info() %}
{{ dim_drawing_by_tenant(tenant_info) }}
```

## Expected Behavior

Fusion should resolve the macro chain (`macro_get_dir_tenant_info()` → dict → `config()`) before validating that `config()` arguments are defined, matching dbt-core's behavior.

## Why This Pattern Exists

In multi-tenant dbt projects, hundreds of tenants share the same SQL logic but each model must output to a **different BigQuery dataset** (`tenant_xxxxxxxx_...`). The `macro_get_dir_tenant_info()` pattern dynamically derives the target dataset from the model's file path, avoiding the need to hardcode dataset names in every model file.

This is a common pattern for large-scale multi-tenant dbt projects. Refactoring away from it is not feasible as it would require hardcoding config in 6,500+ model files.

## What We Tried

- **dbt-autofix**: Cannot fix `dbt1501` errors (only handles deprecation warnings)
- **Manual refactoring**: Not feasible — the dynamic config pattern is architectural (6,500+ files)

## Impact

- Fusion parses in **28.5s** vs dbt-core's **~5 min** (10x improvement) — but **all 6,502 tenant models fail**
- This effectively **blocks Fusion adoption** for any multi-tenant project using dynamic `config()` routing
- Only 72 models parse successfully (non-tenant models)

## Additional Context

The Fusion parse output shows the error occurs during static analysis before macro evaluation:

```
Parse result: 72 successful, 6574 errors (6502 are dbt1501)
```

We believe this is because Fusion tries to validate `config()` arguments at the Jinja template level, before resolving the macro call chain that provides the actual values.

items.body:
## Summary
Identity and tenancy (phase 1: Platform core). Scope, ADRs and exit criteria are in the plan section below.

## Plan
- **Goal.** A caller is a verified person in a tenant, and the database refuses every cross-tenant read and write.
- **Scope.**
  - First ticket: verify the `firebase.tenant` claim name against a real Identity Platform tenant (D14.17).
  - `tenants` and `advisors`; Identity Platform multi-tenancy (one IdP tenant per firm); project-level ID-token verification with firebase-admin and the `firebase.tenant` check (`auth`, ADR-032); `principal` with the 60 s entitlements cache and `entitlement_version`; IdP tenant provisioning script (Terraform comes in E10).
  - Schema for the whole target model in the baseline migration: `documents.raw_content` is dropped here (G-03 early); `acl_change_requests`, `eval_scores`, `turn_events`, `outbox` and `processed_events` tables are created (the outbox is written in E4 and relayed in E5).
  - RLS v2 on all tables: ENABLE + FORCE, SELECT own-or-PUBLIC, writes own-tenant only, PUBLIC writable only by `fa_etl_public`; roles `fa_app` (SELECT only on content), `fa_worker`, `fa_etl`, `fa_etl_public`, `fa_dbt`, `fa_owner`, `fa_lookup`, `fa_maint`, `fa_eval`, `fa_dagster`; `tenants` policies; `advisors` admin-only UPDATE; `advisor_id` owner clauses; `set_config(..., true)` in short transactions; composite FKs.
  - LIST partitions of `chunks` and monthly partitions of `messages` with no partition grants; tenant onboarding in the `migrate` job; `maintenance` job schema and role (scheduling in E10); startup / readiness role and RLS assertions.
  - Leak matrix: reads, writes, FK probes, direct partition access, advisor self-escalation, pooled-connection reuse, fail-closed. Tenant discovery endpoint and `fa_tenant_lookup` (owned by `fa_lookup`).
- **Arch sections.** deep-dive/05-data-model-and-storage.md#5, deep-dive/08-security-and-privacy.md#8.2, deep-dive/04-components-and-responsibilities.md#4.5 (`auth`, `principal`), deep-dive/04-components-and-responsibilities.md#4.8; ADR-002, ADR-003, ADR-004, ADR-010.
- **Dependencies.** E0.
- **Spikes first.** (0, gating, R4) Identity Platform same-email-in-two-tenants spike (about a 5-minute live test, ADR-032): it gates every Identity Platform ticket of this epic (tenant provisioning script, project-level verification with the `firebase.tenant` check, the `advisors` mapping); the docs check of 2026-11-07 found the pages silent, so the live test stays a gate (R4-D18 V5); its result is recorded as an ADR addendum before those tickets start, and a failure switches onboarding to per-firm email aliases with a new ADR. Then: Identity Platform multi-tenancy: confirm billing for > 2 tenants; LIST-partition pruning with the RLS `current_setting` policy plus planner cost at ~52 partitions.
- **Done when.**
  - The L0 leak matrix passes on every PR: cross-tenant read, cross-tenant insert, update and delete into PUBLIC, FK existence probes, direct SELECT / INSERT on a partition as `fa_app` / `fa_worker` gives permission denied, "advisor raises own tier / role" is denied, pooled-connection reuse, unset setting fails closed; leaks = 0.
  - Startup refuses to run when the role is superuser, BYPASSRLS or owner (except the `fa_dbt` and `fa_maint` exemptions), when any tenant table lacks FORCE RLS (including partitioned parents), or when a partition carries a runtime grant (tests).
  - A request with a forged, expired, wrong-audience or wrong-tenant token gets 401; a valid token for tenant A cannot read tenant B rows.
  - `EXPLAIN` shows partition pruning for LIST partitions under RLS.
  - `documents.raw_content` does not exist after the migration; the CI assertion that only `fa_tenant_lookup` is `SECURITY DEFINER` passes.
  - Fixes G-01, G-03, G-12, G-19, G-20, G-21, G-43.

- **Round 4 changes (2026-11-02).**
  - Same-email-in-two-tenants spike gates the Identity Platform tickets (see Spikes first; ADR-032, R4-D11). One IdP tenant per firm, one token per firm, no identity merge; `advisors` has one row per `(tenant_id, idp_uid)`.
  - `tenants` gains `cell_id`, `residency_class`, `llm_egress_ack` (default false) and `active_embed_model`; subject rows (advisors, conversations, messages) carry a random `pseudonym_id` with its mapping table (ADR-031, ADR-038, ADR-035, ADR-029).
  - `principal` compares `home_cell` with this cell and returns 421 plus a cell hint with zero DB reads on a mismatch (ADR-031); the test belongs to E13 (#16).
  - `CREATE EXTENSION btree_gist` (availability on Cloud SQL PG16 UNVERIFIED: check first) and the per-tenant partition-creation migration gives every `chunks` leaf its range columns and its EXCLUDE constraint; new L0 test: every leaf partition has the constraint (ADR-027, R4-D3).
  - Tables owned by E11 to E13 (`document_versions`, `source_registry`, `source_observations`, `deletion_requests`, `erasure_steps`, `lineage_edges`, `embed_generations`) are created by the migration of the epic that owns them, not by this baseline; the startup and CI RLS assertions of this epic cover them automatically (to confirm at planning).
  - Existing done-when bullets stand; the demo multi-tenant setup stays.
  - Validation (2026-11-07, ADR-039): tables with no other owner are named here: E1 owns `pseudonym_map` (created with `advisors`); E11 owns `fund_rr_facts`; E12 owns `erasure_receipts`, `reconciliation_manifests`, `reconciliation_findings` and the PUBLIC `source_purges` table (proposed owners, confirmed at stage 4). `fa_etl_public` gets no write on any firm tenant table: the leak matrix asserts it (ADR-002 D13a stands, ADR-039).

items.body:
## 现象

仓 variable `OPENSHIP_PROJECT_ID = proj_v0QZ68VYDc0pkFxL`，那是 project 名 **`platform-core`**，
跑在 serverId `23a1091e`（219.151.186.106 / 内网 10.0.0.7，**mytech 机**）。

而山海一果生产 `https://platform.shanhaiyiguo.com` 是**另一个** project：
`platform-core-shanhai`（`proj_GLXUtN2bJ92DpPrS`，serverId `8281d598` = 113.249.104.181 / 内网 10.0.0.5）。

⇒ **`ci.yml` 的 deploy job 只覆盖 mytech 实例；山海实例不在自动部署通路上。**

部署史佐证（`GET /projects/proj_GLXUtN2bJ92DpPrS/deployments`）：

- 7 条记录**全部** `trigger: manual`
- 最后一次成功 = **2026-09-23T14:54Z**，commit `93608e54`
- `commit-status`：`deployedSha = 93608e54…`、`latestSha = eecbd65…`、`behind: true`

⇒ main 上 **09-24 之后的合并都没有上这个实例**。

## 已观测到的直接后果

平台镜像里的 `dbt/` 是 09-23 快照（缺 `macros/subject_org.sql`、缺新湖 staging 模型），
而 `scripts/sync-data-semantics.mjs` 读它当 **L1 词表的唯一事实源**

## 为什么开 issue 而不是直接部署

把 main 部署到山海是一次**正式发布**（涉及数十个未上线合并），须单独裁决与验收，不能顺手做。

## 待办

- [ ] 裁决：山海实例纳入自动部署（多 id 怎么表达——每个客户实例各一个仓？还是换个机制），

- [ ] 无论哪种，都要有「这个实例停在哪个 commit」的可见判据——现在只能靠人查 `/commit-status`
- [ ] 正典 / adopt runbook 写清：**仓 variable 只有一个 id，别的实例不会跟着发布**

## 相关

- 公司基建速查里「merge main 即自动部署」那句只对 mytech 实例成立，需订正

items.title: feat: SQL governance policy enforcement (YAML-defined guardrails)
items.body:
## Summary

Port altimate-code's `policy` / SQL governance checks as a new MCP tool (`mcp__opende__check_policy`).

## What it does

Validates SQL against a YAML-defined governance policy — allowed tables, forbidden operations, data access restrictions. Fully deterministic (no LLM). Lets teams encode and enforce SQL standards at the harness level without relying on human review.

## Example policy definition

```yaml
policy:
  forbidden_tables:
    - raw_pii.users
    - raw_pii.payments
  forbidden_operations:
    - DELETE
    - DROP
  required_filters:
    - table: orders
      column: tenant_id
  allowed_schemas:
    - staging
    - marts
```

## Proposed implementation

- New MCP tool `check_policy` accepting `sql` + optional `policy_yaml` / `policy_path`
- Falls back to `.altimate/policy.yml` in the project root
- Returns violations list with severity, rule name, line number
- PR reviewer (`review/run.js`) gains a `policyLane` that runs this check over changed models

## Value

High — this is the only missing deterministic capability with no equivalent in opende today. Governance rules are a common ask in enterprise dbt shops.

items.title: Python models cannot write to Data Warehouse with Service Principal auth (Fabric limitation)

labels.name: upstream-limitation
labels.description: Blocked or limited by upstream dbt / package / platform constraints

labels.name: fabricspark
labels.description: Related to the FabricSpark (Spark SQL / Lakehouse) adapter

items.body:
@sdebruyn 
# Python models fail with Service Principal authentication (two issues)

## Environment

- **dbt-core**: 1.11.2
- **dbt-fabric**: 1.10.1
- **Authentication**: `ActiveDirectoryServicePrincipal`
- **Profile config**: using `workspace_id` + `lakehouse_id` (no `host`)
- **OS**: Windows 11

## Summary

When running Python models with Service Principal (SP) authentication, two separate issues prevent successful execution. SQL models work perfectly with the same SP configuration.

---

## Issue 1: `GET /sessions` returns HTTP 500 with SP token

### Description

`LivySession._get_existing_session()` calls `GET /livyapi/versions/2023-12-01/sessions` to look for a reusable idle session. This endpoint returns **500 Internal Server Error** when authenticated with a Service Principal token, even though the SP has all required Fabric API permissions and workspace roles.

The subsequent `POST /sessions` call works fine (returns 202) with the exact same token.

### Steps to reproduce

```python
from azure.identity import ClientSecretCredential
import requests

credential = ClientSecretCredential(tenant_id="...", client_id="...", client_secret="...")
token = credential.get_token("https://analysis.windows.net/powerbi/api/.default")
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token.token}", "Accept": "application/json"}
base = "https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/workspaces//lakehouses//livyapi/versions/2023-12-01"

# This fails with 500
r1 = requests.get(base + "/sessions", headers=headers)
print("GET:", r1.status_code)  # 500

# This works fine
r2 = requests.post(base + "/sessions", headers=headers, json={"name": "dbt-fabric"})
print("POST:", r2.status_code)  # 202
```

### Workaround

Wrap the GET call in `_get_existing_session()` in a try/except so the adapter falls through to creating a new session:

```python
def _get_existing_session(self) -> str | None:
    try:
        response = requests.get(self._get_base_url() + "/sessions", headers=self._get_headers())
        response.raise_for_status()
        for session in response.json().get("items", []):
            if session["name"] == "dbt-fabric" and session["livyState"] in (
                "idle",
                "starting",
                "running",
            ):
                return session["id"]
    except Exception:
        pass
    return None
```

The only downside is that existing idle sessions won't be reused — a new session is created every time. This is acceptable for most dbt workflows.

### Root cause

This appears to be a Fabric API bug — `GET /sessions` doesn't work with SP tokens while `POST /sessions` does. Worth reporting to Microsoft, but the adapter should handle this gracefully regardless.

---

## Issue 2: `synapsesql` Spark connector does not support Service Principal authentication

### Description

After applying the workaround above, the Livy session is created successfully and the Spark job starts. However, the job itself fails with `InternalServerError` because the generated Spark code uses `spark.read.synapsesql()` and `df.write.synapsesql()` to read from and write to the Fabric Data Warehouse.

**Microsoft explicitly documents that the `synapsesql` connector only supports interactive user authentication — Service Principal is not supported:**

> *"The Spark connector for Fabric Data Warehouse only supports interactive Microsoft Entra user authentication. Service principal authentication isn't supported."*
>
> — [Microsoft Learn: Spark connector for Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/data-engineering/spark-data-warehouse-connector)

### Generated Spark code (from `target/run/`)

```python
import com.microsoft.spark.fabric
from com.microsoft.spark.fabric.Constants import Constants
spark.conf.set("spark.datawarehouse.DW_dbt_club_silver_dev.sqlendpoint", "...,1433")
dbt = dbtObj(spark.read.synapsesql)
df = model(dbt, spark)
df.write.mode("overwrite").synapsesql("DW_dbt_club_silver_dev.mikt.int_accounts_fixed__dbt_tmp")
```

The Spark job starts but fails because `synapsesql` cannot authenticate with the SP identity of the Livy session.

### Error

The Spark monitoring page shows:

```
Status: Failed
Error Code: InternalServerError
Error Message: An internal server error occurred while processing the request.
```

And dbt reports:

```
('42000', "[42000] No item by the name of 'mikt.int_accounts_fixed__dbt_tmp'
could be found in the current database 'DW_dbt_club_silver_dev'")
```

This is because the tmp table was never created — the Spark write failed silently.

### Possible solution

Microsoft provides an alternative Spark connector (`mssql`) that **maybe does** support Service Principal authentication via an explicit access token.

Reference: [Microsoft Learn: Spark connector for SQL databases](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/data-engineering/spark-sql-connector)

The adapter could detect SP authentication and generate Spark code using the `mssql` connector with an explicit access token instead of `synapsesql`. This would require passing the SP credentials into the Spark session (e.g., via `spark.conf.set` or environment variables) so the Spark code can acquire its own token.

---

## What next?

By any chance, have you come across these issues? Do you know any workaround?

Thank you for the great adapter, Sam! Happy to help test any fixes.

items.title: Fix dbt schema tests
items.body:
**Goal:** `dbt test` runs and passes against the real model.

## Context
`dbt-project/models/schema.yml` declares model `person_unified` with columns `tenant_id, legacy_id, name, extra_field`.
Problems:
- The model file is `models/person_unified.sql` but sets `alias='person'`; the output table has no `name` column
  (it has `firstname`, `surname`). The `name` not_null test will error.
- No uniqueness test on the incremental key `(tenant_id, legacy_id)` (the table has `UNIQUE(tenant_id, legacy_id)` in
  `postgres-init/new_system.sql`).
- `schema.yml` source `staging.person_staging` is declared but the SQL does not use `source()`; it selects from
  `person_staging` directly. Either switch the SQL to `{{ source('staging','person_staging') }}` or leave as is.

## Tasks
1. Replace the `name` test with `firstname` and `surname` not_null.

items.title: [E1-T11] Tenant onboarding and advisor seeding in the migrate job
items.body:
## Summary
`migrate --onboard-tenant` creates a tenant's chunks LIST partition with indexes, its tenants row and the IdP mapping, idempotently and without partition grants.

## Description
Implement the onboarding step in the `migrate` entrypoint (E0 created the entrypoint; Cloud Run job, role `fa_owner`): deep-dive/04-components-and-responsibilities.md §4.8 "`migrate` ... tenant onboarding (`--onboard-tenant <slug>`: LIST partition + indexes, `tenants` row, IdP mapping; the IdP tenant itself is provisioned by an onboarding script in E1 ...)". ADR-003: "Tenant onboarding creates its partition and indexes in the `migrate` job."

CLI: `migrate --onboard-tenant <slug> --display-name <name> --idp-tenant-id <id> [--tenant-id <uuid>] [--kind firm|public]`. In one transaction as `fa_owner`: insert the `tenants` row (`status='active'`, new uuid unless `--tenant-id`), call `create_chunks_partition` (E1-T5; partition plus the parent-declared indexes), commit. Rerunning with the same slug is a no-op that exits 0. If rows for that tenant already sit in the DEFAULT partition, exit non-zero with a clear message (do not move rows). The dedicated `eval` tenant is onboarded with `--tenant-id $EVAL_TENANT_ID`. The PUBLIC tenant already exists (E1-T4, E1-T5). Partitions get no grants. Print the new `tenants.id`.

Seed command (R18): `migrate --seed-advisors <file>` reads a JSON file of advisors (`tenant_slug, idp_uid, display_name, role, tier, jurisdictions, licenses`), resolves the tenant by slug, and inserts the `advisors` rows as `fa_owner` (upsert on `(tenant_id, idp_uid)`, idempotent). It is the only way the first advisors are created (demo setup uses it); there is no auto-provision on first login. Unknown tenant slug, invalid tier/role/jurisdiction, or malformed file exits non-zero and inserts nothing.

Out of scope: creating the IdP tenant (E1-T21), Terraform (E10), a tenant-creation HTTP endpoint ("Tenant onboarding (partition creation) is a job, not an endpoint").

Round 4 (ADR-027, ADR-031, ADR-029; deep-dive/04 section 4.8: onboarding creates the LIST partition, indexes, the per-leaf `EXCLUDE` constraint on `chunks`, the `tenants` row including `cell_id`, and the IdP mapping): (1) onboarding takes `--cell-id <cell>` (default: `HOME_CELL` from Settings) and optional `--residency-class none|eu_only|uk_only` and writes them to the `tenants` row. (2) The partition is created through `create_chunks_partition` (E1-T5), so it carries the `EXCLUDE` constraint; after creating it, `migrate` asserts that the new leaf has the constraint and the same indexes as `chunks_public` (like the other partition assertions of section 5.3) and exits non-zero otherwise. (3) `migrate --seed-advisors` also inserts one `pseudonym_map` row per seeded advisor (random `pseudonym_id`, E1-T23), idempotently with the advisor upsert.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given an empty database after migrations, when `migrate --onboard-tenant acme --display-name Acme --idp-tenant-id idp-acme` runs, then `tests/db/test_onboarding.py` passes: one `tenants` row with slug `acme` exists, `chunks` has a partition bound to its id, and `fa_tenant_lookup(p_idp_tenant_id => 'idp-acme')` returns that id.
- [ ] Given the same command is run a second time, then it exits 0 and `SELECT count(*) FROM tenants WHERE slug = 'acme'` is 1 and `chunks` still has exactly one partition for it.
- [ ] Given a chunk inserted for the onboarded tenant by `fa_owner`, then `tableoid::regclass` is the tenant's partition and `chunks_default` is empty (test).
- [ ] Given the new partition, then none of `fa_app, fa_worker, fa_etl, fa_etl_public, fa_dbt, fa_eval` has any privilege on it (`has_table_privilege`), and the same indexes as `chunks_public` exist on it (compared by definition).
- [ ] Given rows of the tenant already in `chunks_default`, when onboarding that tenant runs, then the command exits non-zero and creates no partition.
- [ ] Given a seed file with one valid advisor and one with an unknown `tenant_slug`, when `migrate --seed-advisors` runs, then it exits non-zero and the `advisors` table has no new rows; given only valid entries it inserts them, and a second run leaves the row count unchanged (`tests/db/test_seed_advisors.py`).
- [ ] Given the onboarded partition, then `pg_constraint` shows an exclusion constraint on it and the migrate step's own assertion passes; given a partition created without the constraint (test fixture), then the assertion makes `migrate` exit non-zero (`tests/db/test_onboarding.py::test_leaf_exclude_asserted`).
- [ ] Given `--cell-id eu --residency-class eu_only`, then the `tenants` row has those values; given `--residency-class us_only`, the command exits non-zero and inserts nothing.
- [ ] Given a seed file with two advisors, when `migrate --seed-advisors` runs twice, then `pseudonym_map` has exactly two rows with distinct `pseudonym_id` values and the second run changes none (`tests/db/test_seed_advisors.py::test_pseudonym_rows_seeded_once`).

## Architecture
- deep-dive/04-components-and-responsibilities.md#4.8
- deep-dive/05-1-rls-indexes-versioning-and-deletion.md#5.5
- deep-dive/05-1-rls-indexes-versioning-and-deletion.md#5.10
- deep-dive/05-1-rls-indexes-versioning-and-deletion.md#5.12
- decision-logs.md#adr-003
- decision-logs.md#adr-027
- decision-logs.md#adr-031

- E1-T5
- E1-T9
- E1-T23

items.body:
<!-- pantheon-bus -->
# Pantheon Ops Bus

## Task
- ID: `ODP-BRAND-TRANSFER-IMPLEMENTATION-001`
- Title: 實作真實品牌轉移觀測、freshness 與 SiteScore 消費
- Summary: 實作真實品牌轉移觀測、freshness 與 SiteScore 消費
- Status: `blocked`
- Owner: `Antigravity`
- Reviewer: `Codex`
- Depends On: ODP-BRAND-TRANSFER-CONTRACT-PREP-001, ODP-BRAND-CLASSIFICATION-SYNC-PRESERVATION-001

## Why This Issue Exists
- Reason: H03 盤點結論（2026-09-17，操作者裁示走內部路徑並將 brand_type 修復納入本 task 範圍）。原 H03 判定「repo 內無任何真實品牌轉移資料來源」不精確：消費者跨品牌流動的記錄其實存在，只是被兩處接線缺口擋住。

【已找到的可行資料路徑】ai_consumer_kmeans_v1 的 account 欄位在 apps/data_platform/mapping.py:867-876 被 SHA-256 雜湊為 source_account_ref_hash，落地於 data_plane.learning_import_lineage（infra 的 control_schema.sql 定義，欄位含 source_account_ref_hash、tenant_id、feature_snapshot、run_date）。雜湊具確定性，故同一消費者在不同 tenant 下的記錄可對應，跨品牌轉移即「同一 source_account_ref_hash 出現於多個 tenant_id」，且全程不需解開個資、不需擴大既有投影。feature_snapshot 內含 avgTicket/totalAmount/transCount，可量化轉移金額與次數而非僅有無。來源規模依 apps/data_platform/selection.py:84-91 約 35,307 筆，default_scheduled=True、requires_date_partition=True，asset consumer_segment_import_lineage 採 daily_partitions，即每日更新。tenant 與品牌為 1:1：apps/data_platform/identifiers.py:19 的 brand_id_for_merchant 以 _stable_uuid("owned-brand", source_id) 確定性推導。

【缺口一：brand_type 被硬編抹平】infra/db/migrations 的 core.brands.brand_type 註解明列 owned/franchise/competitor/external 四類，但 apps/data_platform/store.py:1084-1096 於 INSERT 硬編 'owned'，且 ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE 再次強制覆寫 brand_type='owned'、brand_capture_group='fongniao_prod'。任何人工標記的外部或競品品牌都會在下次同步被改回 owned。操作者確認實際存在外部品牌（數量較少），故此缺口直接決定本因子能否涵蓋競品轉移而非僅自我蠶食。修復需同時處理判別依據來源（哪些 merchant 屬 external/franchise/competitor），該依據系統內無現成標記，需業務提供。

【缺口二：消費端未接線】modules/sitescore 的 SiteScoreFeatureInput 無任何品牌轉移欄位；pipelines/dbt 的 brand_transfer_view.sql 為 CROSS JOIN 合成假視圖，硬編 transfer_ratio=0.15 與 data_quality_score=1.0，未被任何生產模組消費。

````markdown
### 3.3.1 Construcción del precio de referencia
Universo de comparación, en este orden y con este peso:
1. **Ofertas de la misión actual** para el mismo `product_key` y especificación compatible (peso alto).
2. **Histórico propio** (`PriceHistory`, últimos 12 meses, mismo `product_key`, especificación compatible).
3. **Benchmark de categoría** (tabla curada al principio; ClickHouse + dbt en fase 3).

Magnitud comparada: **landed cost por unidad normalizado a EUR**, no el precio de listado. Dos ofertas
con el mismo precio y envíos distintos no son comparables.

Se exige un tamaño de muestra mínimo `sanity.min_sample` (por defecto **5**). Si no se alcanza, el
resultado es `insufficient_reference` y la oferta **va a gate humano**: no se negocia a ciegas.
````

</details>

<details><summary>Spec excerpt: 5.5 Datos</summary>

````markdown
## 5.5 Datos
- **PostgreSQL 16** transaccional, multi-tenant por `tenant_id` con **RLS**.
- **Prisma** (desde `web`) y **SQLAlchemy 2 + Alembic** (desde `orchestrator`) sobre **el mismo esquema**,
  con un único paquete dueño de las migraciones para evitar deriva.
- **pgvector** para embeddings (productos, histórico de negociaciones, catálogos).
- **Redis** para caché, colas, rate limiting, estado efímero de sesión de navegador y **sesiones de firma**.
- **S3-compatible** (MinIO local / R2 o S3 en producción) para capturas, PDFs, adjuntos de chat, CSV
  originales y **almacenamiento WORM (Object Lock) del log de auditoría firmado**.
- **ClickHouse** (fases 2-3) para precios históricos y benchmarks que alimentan el precio de referencia de
  3.3.1; **dbt** para los marts de precios y ahorro.
````

</details>

items.title: [platform] §9.1 Plaid financial data integration: Link flow, transaction sync webhook handling, plaid schema DDL, and cash flow normalization into accounting schema

labels.name: spec
labels.description: Spec-driven issue derived from engineering-spec-v1.0 or Blueprint v1.8

items.body:
---
owner: platform
depends_on: [1026, 1027, 1018]
blocks: [1077, 1086]
spec_sections: ["§9.1"]
blueprint_sections: ["§17"]
maturity_target: foundation
acceptance:
  - Plaid products enabled: Auth, Transactions, Income, Liabilities, Assets, Identity; sandbox environment wired for local development
  - Link flow: server-side link_token creation at POST /v1/plaid/link-token; client Plaid Link UI renders with token; on success, public token exchanged for access token server-side only; access token stored encrypted in integration.connections
  - plaid schema DDL: plaid.items (item_id, org_id, tenant_id, institution_id, access_token_encrypted, status), plaid.accounts (item_id, account_id, name, type, subtype, mask, current_balance, available_balance), plaid.transactions (account_id, transaction_id, date, amount, category, merchant_name, pending) with TimescaleDB hypertable partitioning by date
  - Webhook handler: POST /v1/plaid/webhook validates Plaid-Verification-Header; handles TRANSACTIONS_REMOVED (soft-delete transactions), SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE (trigger transaction sync job), ITEM_ERROR (mark item disconnected, notify user)
  - Transaction sync job: Inngest function processes SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE events; calls /transactions/sync with cursor; upserts added/modified, marks removed; updates plaid.items.last_sync_at
  - Cash flow normalization: dbt model or service layer aggregates plaid.transactions into accounting schema (monthly revenue, COGS, operating expenses, net cash flow); feeds Diagnostic Engine financial domain
  - Reconnection flow: when item enters error state, user sees reconnection prompt in Client Workspace vault surface; re-links with Plaid Link Update Mode
  - Plaid data in BAI: plaid cash flow signals included in BPFS feature vector (avg_monthly_revenue, cash_flow_volatility, days_of_cash); injected into BAI decision envelope
---

## Details

Per Spec §9.1, Plaid provides bank account connection, transaction history, income, liabilities, assets, and identity verification. Issue #1077 covers HUSLFi Plaid-integrated financial intelligence (the HUSLFi layer), but the core Plaid integration — Link flow, webhook handling, plaid schema DDL, transaction sync job, and cash flow normalization into the accounting schema — has no dedicated tracking.

Plaid is the primary live financial data source. Without this tracked separately, the integration risks being built in a fragmented way across HUSLFi, vault, and diagnostic surfaces without a unified data persistence layer.

**Spec sections:** §9.1, Blueprint §17 (HUSLFi infrastructure)

items.title: Phase 5 — Data Platform, BI, IA éducative et reporting institutionnel
items.body:
## Objectif
Transformer SchoolFlow Pro en plateforme data-driven : entrepôt analytique, tableaux de bord BI, indicateurs institutionnels, IA éducative, scoring étudiant, prédiction du décrochage, reporting ministère et pilotage stratégique.

Cette phase doit capitaliser sur les phases précédentes : production, sécurité, observabilité, SaaS, quotas et multi-tenant.

---

## Périmètre Phase 5

### 1. Data warehouse éducatif
- Créer une couche analytique séparée de l’OLTP opérationnel.
- Préparer schémas `bronze`, `silver`, `gold` ou équivalent.
- Construire des marts analytiques : élèves, inscriptions, présences, notes, finances, enseignants, campus, paiements.
- Prévoir refresh incrémental.
- Ne pas ralentir la base opérationnelle.

### 2. Modèle décisionnel BI
- Créer dimensions : date, tenant, campus, classe, niveau, programme, matière, enseignant, élève, parent, statut paiement.
- Créer faits : inscriptions, présences, notes, factures, paiements, absences, incidents, communications, connexions.
- Préparer modèle étoile compatible Superset/Metabase/Power BI.

### 3. Dashboards Superset / BI
- Dashboard direction établissement.
- Dashboard finance scolaire.
- Dashboard pédagogique.
- Dashboard présence/absentéisme.
- Dashboard multi-campus.
- Dashboard ministère / institution : indicateurs agrégés anonymisés.
- Dashboard SaaS platform usage si nécessaire.

### 4. Indicateurs clés éducatifs
- Taux de présence.
- Taux d’absentéisme.
- Moyenne par classe/matière/campus.
- Taux de réussite.
- Taux d’impayés.
- Recouvrement financier.
- Charge enseignants.
- Risque décrochage.
- Evolution inscriptions.
- Performance par période académique.

### 5. IA éducative
- Résumé automatique d’un élève.
- Recommandations pédagogiques.
- Détection d’élèves à risque.
- Aide à la rédaction de bulletins/commentaires.
- Assistant direction : synthèse activité établissement.
- Assistant parent : explication simple des notes/absences.
- Assistant enseignant : suggestions d’accompagnement.

### 6. ML prédictif
- Scoring risque décrochage.
- Scoring impayés.
- Prédiction absentéisme.
- Détection anomalies notes/paiements.
- Modèle simple au départ : règles + features SQL.
- Evolution future : scikit-learn / XGBoost / MLflow.

### 7. Gouvernance et confidentialité
- Anonymisation pour reporting institutionnel.
- Séparation données opérationnelles et analytiques.
- RLS analytique par tenant/campus/rôle.
- Masquage PII dans les vues ministère.
- Journalisation des exports BI.

### 8. Pipelines data
- Préparer jobs ETL/ELT async ou DBT.
- Option 1 : vues matérialisées PostgreSQL.
- Option 2 : dbt + PostgreSQL analytique.
- Option 3 futur : Airflow + warehouse séparé.
- Ajouter tests de qualité data : unicité, non-null, cohérence référentielle.

---

## Règles de sécurité
- Ne jamais exposer PII entre tenants.
- Les dashboards institutionnels doivent être anonymisés/agrégés.
- Les modèles IA ne doivent pas utiliser des données d’un tenant pour répondre à un autre tenant.
- Les exports doivent être journalisés.
- Toute vue analytique doit être filtrable par tenant ou explicitement globale/anonymisée.

---

## Découpage recommandé en PR

### PR 1 — Cadrage modèle analytique
- Ajouter `docs/data/ANALYTICS_MODEL.md`.
- Définir dimensions, faits, KPIs, règles de confidentialité.

### PR 2 — Vues analytiques PostgreSQL MVP
- Ajouter vues/matérialisées pour dashboard direction : élèves, présences, finances, notes.
- Ajouter migration non destructive.

### PR 3 — Data quality tests
- Ajouter tests SQL/pytest sur cohérence analytique.
- Vérifier tenant_id, dates, montants, statuts.

### PR 4 — Dashboard API analytics
- Ajouter endpoints API dashboard analytiques optimisés.
- Prévoir cache Redis court.

### PR 5 — Superset/BI pack
- Ajouter documentation connexion Superset.
- Ajouter datasets recommandés.
- Préparer export dashboard JSON si possible.

### PR 6 — IA éducative MVP
- Ajouter service de résumé élève.
- Ajouter garde-fous PII/tenant.
- Utiliser Groq/OpenRouter uniquement si clé configurée.

### PR 7 — Scoring risque décrochage V1
- Règles simples : absentéisme, baisse notes, impayés, retards.
- Score explicable, non bloquant.
- Dashboard alertes.

### PR 8 — Reporting institutionnel anonymisé
- Vues agrégées par région/campus/niveau/période.
- Pas de nom/prénom/email/téléphone.
- Documentation conformité.

---

## Critères d’acceptation
- Les données analytiques ne ralentissent pas les workflows opérationnels.
- Les KPIs direction sont disponibles avec cache ou vues optimisées.
- Les vues BI respectent le tenant isolation.
- Superset peut se connecter à un modèle propre sans requêter directement toutes les tables OLTP.
- Les premiers scores IA/ML sont explicables et non décisionnels.
- Le reporting institutionnel est anonymisé.
- Les exports analytiques sont traçables.

items.title: dbt: two staged events for one key in a batch wedge the pipeline (duplicate key)
items.body:
## Problem
If two staged events for the same `(tenant_id, legacy_id)` land in one dbt batch, `person_unified.sql` (incremental) hits
`person_tenant_id_legacy_id_key` ("duplicate key value violates unique constraint"). The batch is never marked processed,
so every later `dbt run` retries the same batch and fails: the pipeline is wedged until someone intervenes. Already known
from #4 (the `poisons_stack` xfails); this ticket tracks the fix.

## New evidence (found while working #12)
`make test-resilience` on branch `issue-12-offset-commit-after-failed-stage`: `test_offset_replay__verify` fails. After the
offset reset the consumer replays all history; `tenant_a1` id 5 appears twice in Kafka (staged at 11:04:07 and 11:04:24
in the preceding `legacy_down` scenario, probably Debezium re-emitting the row after the legacy DB restarted), so both
events are in one batch. Postgres logs the duplicate key error, `dbt transformation failed:` follows (blank, see below),
and the canary row never reaches `person`. So a normal offset replay can trigger it, not just rapid updates.

## Suggested fix
In the model, reduce each batch to the latest staged event per `(tenant_id, source_id)` (e.g. `row_number() over
(partition by tenant_id, source_id order by id desc) = 1`) before the incremental merge/insert. Check DELETE handling at
the same time (DELETE events are currently dead-lettered, see #12), since "latest event wins" must not resurrect a deleted row.

Small related improvement: `run_dbt_transformation` prints `result.stderr`, but dbt writes errors to stdout, so failures are
logged blank. Log the tail of stdout too.

## Done when
- [ ] Two events for one key in one batch no longer fail `dbt run` (dbt model test in `tests/dbt`).
- [ ] The `poisons_stack` xfails in `tests/e2e/test_edge_cases.py` that this fixes are removed (strict xfail will tell us which).
- [ ] `test_offset_replay__verify` passes on a stack that has had the legacy-down scenario run before it.

Related: #4, #12.

[Table partitioning](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/11/ddl-partitioning.html) has existed since PostgreSQL 9, but in PostgreSQL 11 has been made significantly easier to use and more performant.

Anyone who has solid Medium-Sized™ data that doesn't quite need the complexity or resources provided by BigQuery/RedShift/Snowflake.

items.title: Authorized-view warning cannot tell tenant-safe views from leaking ones
items.body:
## Problem

`server/src/spec_validator.cpp` (~477-482) warns "does not reference a key variable" for every initSQL authorized view whose body does not mention a key variable such as `:tenant_id`.

However, initSQL does not bind `:tenant_id` (it fails at warmup), and authorized views are not wrapped by the rewriter's tenant filter. The only correct way to isolate a view over a shared table is therefore a literal predicate written by the SaaS, e.g. `WHERE tenant_id = 21`, in a spec generated for that one sandbox.

As a result:
- the warning fires on correctly filtered views and on leaking views alike, so it cannot distinguish a safe view from an unsafe one;
- it does not explain how to fix the problem;
- duckbox does not check that the literal matches the sandbox key. Reusing one spec for several keys (e.g. a view with `tenant_id = 21` created under key `tenant_22`) silently exposes tenant 21's rows to tenant 22. This was reproduced via the daemon with ADBC during the PR #7 review.

## Proposal

- Analyze the bound plan of each authorized view and detect an equality predicate on the spec's tenant column.
- Require that predicate's value to equal the tenant id derived from the sandbox key. If it differs, reject CreateSandbox/UpdateSandbox (strict mode, the default for production) with a message naming the view, the column, the literal, and the expected value.
- A view over a shared table with no tenant predicate: error in strict mode, and an actionable warning otherwise.
- Provide an explicit spec flag for views over single-tenant tables, so the check can be skipped intentionally and visibly.
- Alternatively, or additionally, let initSQL views reference the sandbox's tenant id safely (e.g. a trusted, frozen setting/variable resolved at warmup), so specs don't need literals at all.

## Acceptance

- A view with `WHERE <tenant_column> = <literal>` where the literal equals the sandbox key's tenant id: no warning.
- The same view under a different key: CreateSandbox and UpdateSandbox fail in strict mode.
- A view over a shared table without a tenant predicate: error in strict mode, clear warning otherwise.
- Tests cover all three cases, through the daemon with two sandboxes/keys.

items.title: Team folders: Implement metrics to track current usage for users
items.body:
Metric: TTFV (Time To First Value) for new users — first login ➜ first meaningful dashboard interaction

## Why
We want to quantify how long it takes a new user to reach value after they first log in to Grafana. This supports the department’s Consumption (50‑90‑90) and Adoption goals and the emphasis on first‑session success (“consider a team and an individual’s first login…onboard quickly”). TTFV will sit alongside TTRD (Time to right dashboard, coming later) as a top outcome metric for activation.  ￼  ￼

## What
Definition we'll use:
- Start (first login): a user’s first successful login in a tenant (org) — “first ever” in that tenant.
- End (first meaningful dashboard interaction): the first of:
  - a dashboard.interaction event (refresh panel, edit, star, share, time‑range change, etc.), or
  - dwell ≥ 30s on a dashboard after a dashboard.view (same rule you use for TTRD). 
- Metric(s):
  - TTFV p95 / p50 (seconds) among users who reached “value” within a window (e.g., 24h of first login).
  - TTFV success rate: % of first‑login users who reached value within 24h (and within 7 days).
- Scope: “New user in existing stack” is the primary lens (most impact). We’ll also tag “brand‑new stack” first sessions when detectable from environment flags (secondary). 
  - can we segment on 'new stack' vs 'new user in existing stack' or should we delay that until later?

Out of scope:
- Deeper onboarding experiments — this ticket is measurement only to unblock those.

## Acceptance criteria
1. we have instrumented what's necessary to measure the metric
   - PII Concerns: event payloads include hashed/stable IDs only; no auth tokens or email addresses or other PII is logged.
2. Data model - we dont need to worry about modeling in this ticket. Focus on getting a first cut of these metrics in dashboards, model in dbt is optional. Future models we may like: fct_user_first_login, fct_user_first_value, fct_ttfv_users to report on.
3. Dashboard - a dashboard panel showing TTFV p95 (last 7/14 days) - breakdown of new vs existing stack optional.
4. Validation - Manual QA: pick 10 new users and verify their first login and first value timestamps match expected replay (FullStory link) and internal logs. I'm unsure what's possible here based on what we have access to.

## Imp notes
1. events
   - what login success event do we use? 
   - we'll need dashboard view and interact events if they dont exist. **We need to decide on what interact events matter here, like: refresh, edit, star, share, time_range_change, …?**
2. first login - do we have this in the warehouse already? Can the backend emit it? We might need to guess on this i there isnt a fact table today. Down the line, likely not within this ticket, would be to define a fact table for this if it does not exist.
3. first value -     - interaction_ts = MIN(dashboard.interaction.ts) on/after first_login_ts.    - dwell_ts = dashboard.view.ts + 30s when the time until the next event is ≥ 30s.      - might need new telemetry for the dwell window? or query for non-existence of another event in that window.
    - first_value_ts = LEAST(interaction_ts, dwell_ts) (whichever exists).
    - Compute ttfv_sec = first_value_ts − first_login_ts.
    - Mark success if first_value_ts exists; also compute flags for within 24h and within 7d.

## More future ideas
We could value building these in the future:
- A cohort table: TTFV by team count, plan, or tenant size (as data allows, but we could request it).
- full modeling of fct tables as noted above.
- Add joins to dim_team and dim_dashboard (but those dont exist yet) to segment TTFV by team, service, datasource, etc. 

## Snippet of example query from LLM!
```sql
WITH first_login AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, user_id, MIN(ts) AS first_login_ts
  FROM `project.dataset.auth_login_success`
  GROUP BY tenant_id, user_id
),
events AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, user_id, event_name, dashboard_id, ts,
         LEAD(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY tenant_id, user_id ORDER BY ts) AS next_ts
  FROM `project.dataset.events`
  WHERE event_name IN ('dashboard.view','dashboard.interaction')
),
first_value AS (
  SELECT
    fl.tenant_id, fl.user_id, fl.first_login_ts,
    MIN(
      CASE
        WHEN e.event_name = 'dashboard.interaction' AND e.ts >= fl.first_login_ts THEN e.ts
        WHEN e.event_name = 'dashboard.view' AND e.ts >= fl.first_login_ts
             AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(COALESCE(e.next_ts, TIMESTAMP_ADD(e.ts, INTERVAL 1 DAY)), e.ts, SECOND) >= 30
        THEN TIMESTAMP_ADD(e.ts, INTERVAL 30 SECOND)
      END
    ) AS first_value_ts
  FROM first_login fl
  LEFT JOIN events e
    ON e.tenant_id = fl.tenant_id AND e.user_id = fl.user_id
  GROUP BY fl.tenant_id, fl.user_id, fl.first_login_ts
),
ttfv AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id, user_id, first_login_ts, first_value_ts,
    CASE WHEN first_value_ts IS NOT NULL THEN TIMESTAMP_DIFF(first_value_ts, first_login_ts, SECOND) END AS ttfv_sec,
    CASE WHEN first_value_ts IS NOT NULL AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(first_value_ts, first_login_ts, HOUR) <= 24 THEN TRUE END AS success_24h,
    CASE WHEN first_value_ts IS NOT NULL AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(first_value_ts, first_login_ts, DAY)  <= 7  THEN TRUE END AS success_7d
  FROM first_value
)
SELECT
  DATE(first_login_ts) AS dt,
  COUNT(*) AS new_users,
  SUM(CASE WHEN success_24h THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS reached_value_24h,
  SUM(CASE WHEN success_7d  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS reached_value_7d,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(ttfv_sec, 100)[OFFSET(50)] AS ttfv_p50_sec,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(ttfv_sec, 100)[OFFSET(95)] AS ttfv_p95_sec
FROM ttfv
GROUP BY dt
ORDER BY dt;
```
