<details><summary>Spec excerpt: 3.4 Confianza del vendedor (acompaña a toda oferta y a toda decisión)</summary>

````markdown
## 3.4 Confianza del vendedor (acompaña a toda oferta y a toda decisión)

**Requisito de producto:** cada oferta, cada trato y cada decisión firmada lleva asociado un
`SellerConfidence` con su banda y su explicación. No es un adorno del perfil del vendedor: es un criterio
de filtrado y de auditoría.

El cálculo es **determinista y versionado** (`model_version`). El LLM no puntúa vendedores; como máximo
redacta la explicación a partir de las señales ya normalizadas.

### 3.4.1 Señales de entrada (estructuradas, del adapter)

| Grupo | Señales |
|---|---|
| **Antigüedad** | `account_age_days`, `first_sale_date`, `months_active_last_12` |
| **Ventas** | `lifetime_transactions`, `transactions_12m`, `gmv_12m`, `repeat_buyer_share` |
| **Catálogo** | `published_products_count`, `catalog_churn_30d`, `spec_completeness_avg` |
| **Reseñas** | `reviews_total`, `reviews_12m`, `rating_avg`, `rating_count`, `verified_review_share`, `response_rate` |
| **Garantía institucional** | `identity_verified` (KYC), `trade_assurance`, `escrow_available`, `dispute_rate`, `refund_rate` |
| **Calidad del dato** | `data_completeness` (señales presentes / señales requeridas) |

Cada `PlatformAdapter` devuelve estas señales crudas; la normalización a un esquema común es
responsabilidad del `TrustAgent`, nunca del adapter.

### 3.4.2 Cálculo (cuatro pasos, todos deterministas)

**Paso 1 — Normalización saturada.** Cada señal se lleva a [0,1] con funciones documentadas y monótonas.
Los conteos (ventas, productos, reseñas) usan escala logarítmica saturada:
`f(x) = log10(1 + x) / log10(1 + x_sat)`, acotada a 1, con `x_sat` configurable por señal. La antigüedad
usa saturación lineal con techo (`seller.age_saturation_days`, defecto 730).

**Paso 2 — Suavizado bayesiano del rating.** Un vendedor con una reseña de 5,0 no puede puntuar por
encima de uno con 500 reseñas a 4,8. Se aplica shrinkage hacia la media de la categoría:

```
rating_adj = (C * m + rating_avg * rating_count) / (C + rating_count)
# C = seller.rating_prior_weight (defecto 25), m = media de la categoría
```

Para la proporción de reseñas positivas se usa además el **límite inferior de Wilson** (95%), que premia
la evidencia abundante sobre la escasa.

**Paso 3 — Penalizaciones y topes.**
- `data_completeness < seller.min_signals` → banda `insufficient_data`, score no calculado.
- **Detección de manipulación de reseñas** (rúbrica determinista sobre estructura, no sobre texto libre):
  ráfaga de reseñas con z-score de velocidad superior a `seller.review_burst_z` (defecto 3.0); proporción
  de 5 estrellas anómala frente a la distribución esperada de la categoría; `verified_review_share` muy
  bajo; textos duplicados o genéricos; picos de reseñas correlacionados con la fecha de creación de la
  cuenta. Cualquier flag activo **capa la banda**: el vendedor no puede superar `low` aunque el resto de
  señales sean excelentes. No se resta puntos: se acota. Un vendedor que infla reseñas no debe poder
  compensarlo con volumen.
- `dispute_rate` o `refund_rate` por encima de `seller.max_dispute_rate` → penalización proporcional.

**Paso 4 — Score y banda.**
`score = round(100 * Σ w_i · f_i)` con pesos por grupo (antigüedad, ventas, catálogo, reseñas, garantía
institucional) configurables por tenant y categoría. Las señales de garantía institucional ponderan más que
las de volumen.

| Banda | Rango (defecto) | Efecto |
|---|---|---|
| `high` | score ≥ 75 | negociación y compra con normalidad |
| `medium` | 50 ≤ score < 75 | negociación normal; confirmación adicional si el importe supera `approval.threshold` |
| `low` | 25 ≤ score < 50 | **gate humano obligatorio** aunque el precio sea normal; no puede ser recomendación nº1 |
| `untrusted` | score < 25 o por debajo de `seller.hard_block_below` | **descartar**, salvo override firmado y justificado |
| `insufficient_data` | señales insuficientes | **gate humano**, con aviso explícito de "vendedor sin historial suficiente" |

### 3.4.3 Frescura y versionado
El snapshot se recalcula antes de cada decisión si tiene más de `seller.snapshot_max_age_days` (defecto 30)
días. Se conserva el histórico de snapshots (`SellerSignalSnapshot` + `SellerConfidence`) para poder
reconstruir qué se sabía en cada momento. Cambiar pesos o umbrales genera nueva `model_version` y es una
decisión firmada; las evaluaciones guardan la versión usada para ser reproducibles.

### 3.4.4 Combinación con la banda de precio (regla de escalada)

La confianza **no se compensa con el precio**. Reglas duras:

| Precio \ Confianza | `high` / `medium` | `low` / `insufficient_data` | `untrusted` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `normal` | negociar | **gate humano** | **descartar** |
| `atypical` | gate humano | **escalar a descarte** (`implausible`) | **descartar** |
| `implausible` | descartar | descartar | descartar |

- Precio anómalamente barato **y** vendedor poco fiable es la señal de fraude más informativa del sistema:
  sube un nivel de severidad, no se diluye en una media ponderada.
- El descarte por esta regla siempre es visible y reversible solo mediante override firmado que queda en
  el log de auditoría con su motivo.
- El importe final del trato y su `SellerConfidence` viajan juntos en el payload firmado, de modo que la
  decisión es auditable contra el conocimiento disponible en ese instante.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Ofertas normalizadas] --> B[SellerConfidence]
  A --> C[PriceSanityCheck]
  B --> D{Combinar 3.4.4}
  C --> D
  D -- normal + confiable --> N[Negociar]
  D -- zona gris --> G[Gate humano]
  D -- descarte --> X[Descartar + motivo]
  N --> R[Reclasificar con precio negociado]
  R --> D
```
````

</details>

<details><summary>Spec excerpt: 10. ROADMAP</summary>

````markdown
# 10. ROADMAP

**Fase 0 — Cimientos (3-4 semanas).** Monorepo, CI, auth, multi-tenant, esquema de datos, motor monetario
multi-divisa y FX, **infraestructura de firmas (Ed25519, JCS, cadena de hashes, WORM, sesión de firma de 15
minutos)**, **`LLMGateway` compatible OpenAI con stub en CI**, observabilidad y contratos OpenAPI.

**Fase 1 — MVP honesto (8-10 semanas).** Onboarding con **importador CSV financiero**. Dos
`PlatformAdapter` (una vía API oficial si existe, una vía scraping) devolviendo señales de vendedor.
**`TrustAgent` con suavizado bayesiano, bandas y detección de manipulación** y `SanityAgent` con bandas
configurables; matriz de escalada 3.4.4 implementada. `FinanceAgent` con landed cost multimoneda.
`EvaluatorAgent` con MCDA y explicación. **Dashboard de tratos y cola de gate con decisiones firmadas y
sesión de firma.** **Negociación semi-automática** (el agente redacta, el humano aprueba cada envío)
contra el servidor de chat simulado. Sin pagos.

**Fase 2 — Negociación autónoma (6-8 semanas).** Envío autónomo con guardarraíles en una plataforma real,
takeover humano, renegociación desde dashboard, doble control de firmas, memoria de precios, aprobaciones,
RFQ y orden de compra en PDF con certificado de firmas y confianza del vendedor. Tercera y cuarta
plataforma.

**Fase 3 — Inteligencia (6 semanas).** ClickHouse + dbt para benchmarks que alimentan el precio de
referencia; calibración del modelo de confianza con datos reales por categoría; resolución de identidad de
vendedor entre plataformas; proyección de tesorería multiperiodo desde históricos CSV; modelos
autoalojados en producción para extracción y clasificación.

**Fase 4 — Escala.** Más plataformas como plugins, SSO empresarial, SLA, anclaje externo de auditoría
(RFC 3161), playbooks de negociación por categoría y conexión bancaria PSD2 opcional como mejora sobre el CSV.
````

</details>

items.title: M5-32 — Ingest campaign placement bidding config, then restore a real set_placement_modifier rule
items.body:
**Backlog ref:** carved out of #27 (ADR 005)

## Why this exists

#27 wired the `placement` scope and turned `flag_low_cvr_placement` into a diagnostic. It did **not** restore the ability to actually change a placement modifier, and that was deliberate.

A placement bid adjustment is a **percentage on top of whatever the campaign already has**. The old rule carried `{"op": "add_pct", "delta_pct": -20}`, but the current modifier lives in campaign config (`dynamicBidding.placementBidding`) and **nothing ingests it**. So:

- there is no `before_value` to compute from;
- assuming `0%` is right until the day the seller had set `+50%` by hand, at which point "lower it 20%" becomes "wipe their decision";
- the reason text shown to the approver would have been a lie, and apply-time drift detection would only catch it *after* a human approved a false premise.

So `mart_ppc_placement_daily.placement_modifier_pct` is published as `null::numeric` on purpose. `services/ingest/clients/ads_api.py::update_placement_modifier` refuses when `current_percentage is None`. This issue removes that null.

## Scope

1. **New raw dataset for campaign config.** This is **state, not a daily fact** — a modifier has no report date. It needs its own shape (current-state snapshot with a `captured_at`, or an SCD-2 table), not a row per day appended forever.
2. **Staging + mart column**: replace the `null::numeric` in `mart_ppc_placement_daily` with the real modifier, joined per `(tenant_id, campaign_id, placement)`.
3. **Off-Amazon has no modifier.** `placement_api_enum` is already `NULL` for `off_amazon` and `unknown`. A rule must never propose a modifier where the enum is null — Amazon has nothing to set.
4. **Restore a mutating rule** (a new code, e.g. `reduce_low_cvr_placement_modifier`) in `starter_rules.py`, keeping `flag_low_cvr_placement` as the report-only version for accounts that stay manual.
5. **Clamp the modifier range.** Amazon caps placement adjustments; the guardrail `BOUNDS` check needs min/max for this action type, and `set_placement_modifier` is already in the `action_type` CHECK from `0006`.
6. **Write-back** in `update_placement_modifier` (currently `NotImplementedError`), including reading the live value at apply time so a hand edit between proposal and approval fails as `drift:` rather than overwriting.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Campaign placement-bidding config is ingested for a tenant, with a captured-at timestamp
- [ ] `mart_ppc_placement_daily.placement_modifier_pct` is non-null for campaigns that have a modifier set, and 0 (not null) for campaigns explicitly at 0%
- [ ] `dbt build` passes, including a test that the modifier is null **only** where `placement_api_enum` is null
- [ ] A mutating placement rule exists, seeded disabled + dry-run, and `test_every_catalog_rule_has_a_wired_scope` still passes
- [ ] A dry-run produces a proposal whose `before_value` came from Amazon, not from a default
- [ ] `update_placement_modifier` still raises when the current value is unknown (regression test)
- [ ] Gate command output pasted into a comment on this issue

## Closure rule (#31)

Code pushed is not done. This closes only when the gate command has actually run, its output is in a comment here, and every box above is ticked.

## Blocked by

- #8 (Ads API access) — nothing can be ingested before credentials exist.
- Realistically also #22 (approval queue + write-back), since a modifier change is a write-back action.

items.title: Design: agent-context contract for dbt entities, policy, time, and provenance

labels.name: usecase: economic-data-project
labels.description: Supports the economic-data-project proof of concept or production adoption

items.body:
Parent: #132
Extends: #86
Blocks: #146, #147
Related: #133, #135, #139, #141, #144

## Outcome

Define a versioned agent-context contract that lets retrieved documents and chunks join reliably to dbt entities and be queried with exact temporal, authorization, freshness, provenance, and citation semantics.

This extends #86's document registry, section, chunk, extraction, and embedding grains. It does not replace the dbt Semantic Layer or create a second metrics system.

The contract is the bridge between:

- quantitative data and entities queried through dbt and dbt MCP; and
- governed documentary context built and served by dbt-ml.

## Recommended relational shape

Extend the #86 outputs and add a normalized many-to-many link relation:

### `document_registry`

One row per logical document version, including stable logical identity, source version, time, freshness, policy, and provenance.

### `document_chunks`

One row per indexable chunk, including stable chunk identity, document version, citation locator, carried policy fields, and transformation provenance.

### `context_entity_links`

One row per document/chunk-to-dbt-entity relationship:

- `context_id`;
- `entity_namespace` and `entity_name`;
- `entity_id` or a canonically serialized typed key/value;
- originating dbt resource `unique_id` where available;
- relationship type, link method, and provenance;
- optional confidence for inferred links.

Retrieval projections may denormalize fields needed for filtering, but the warehouse relations remain the auditable system of record.

## Required contract semantics

### Stable identity

Define exact, testable generation rules for:

- `document_id`: logical identity across source versions;
- `document_version_id`: immutable content/source version;
- `chunk_id`: stable while canonical chunk content and locator identity are unchanged;
- `context_id`: stable retrieval-record identity;
- `entity_id`: namespaced stable identity compatible with a dbt Semantic Layer entity key.

IDs must be adapter-independent and safe for incremental merge, deletion, citation resolution, and retrieval publication.

### Bitemporal validity

Use UTC timestamps and half-open intervals:

- `valid_from` / `valid_to`: when the context applies in business time;
- `recorded_from` / `recorded_to`: when that version was known to the system.

A null upper bound means open-ended. The contract must define how an unknown effective date differs from open-ended validity and how a consumer performs reproducible “as of” queries.

### Permissions

Indexable context must carry typed, filterable authorization attributes such as:

- `tenant_id`;
- `is_public`;
- `access_groups`;
- `classification` or `policy_ref`;
- policy source/version provenance.

Missing or unresolved authorization metadata is deny-by-default. Mandatory policy filters are derived from trusted caller claims at retrieval time and cannot be weakened by an LLM or user-supplied relevance filter. ACL-only changes must invalidate and republish affected rows according to #139.

### Freshness

Define at least:

- source update/observation time;
- ingestion time;
- materialization time;
- last freshness check;
- optional `stale_after`.

Consumers must be able to distinguish an old-but-valid document from a pipeline that has stopped refreshing.

### Provenance

Records must retain safe identifiers or hashes for:

- source system and URI;
- source content/version;
- parser, chunker, transform, prompt, schema, provider, and model versions where applicable;
- upstream dbt/dbt-ml node `unique_id`;
- invocation or materialization run.

### Citation locator

A retrieval result must resolve to an exact document version and human-verifiable location. Support common typed fields such as:

- page number;
- section path or heading;
- character offsets;
- speaker and timestamp for transcripts;
- source URI.

A flexible locator payload may supplement these fields, but must not be the only representation of commonly filtered or rendered values.

## SQL and artifact integration

SQL models from #141 should be able to build entity links, effective-date intervals, and policy projections without moving warehouse data through Python.

The manifest and `emit-dbt-sources` output must expose the contract version, grains, keys, lineage, and safe relation names so downstream dbt projects and MCP tools can discover them mechanically.

## Product boundary

dbt-ml owns the context schema, build-time lineage, provenance, freshness metadata, and policy-bearing retrieval records.

dbt/dbt MCP owns metric and structured-data querying. A retrieval server owns enforcement of mandatory policy filters using trusted caller identity. dbt-ml is not an identity provider, authorization decision service, entity-resolution platform, conventional metrics semantic layer, or answer-generation framework.

Agent consumption is in scope as a data-plane contract; agent reasoning and orchestration remain outside the core.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A versioned `agent_context/v1` contract documents every field, grain, nullability rule, and identifier algorithm.
- [ ] One document version can link multiple chunks to multiple dbt entities without duplicating the source-of-record document rows.
- [ ] Business-time and system-time “as of” selection is deterministic and covered by interval tests.
- [ ] Missing policy metadata is denied, and ACL-only updates invalidate retrieval projections.
- [ ] Freshness fields distinguish source age from pipeline-refresh failure.
- [ ] Every search result can round-trip to its document version, exact citation locator, entity links, and source-to-index lineage.
- [ ] Manifest/docs and `emit-dbt-sources` expose the contract without credentials or sensitive caller claims.
- [ ] DuckDB fixtures cover stable IDs, version replacement, entity links, interval boundaries, ACL changes, stale records, citation resolution, and provenance.
- [ ] The contract can be constructed by a SQL model compatible with #141 and published using #139's record-level state semantics.

## Out of scope

- Defining metrics, measures, or Semantic Layer query semantics.
- Authenticating users or issuing identity claims.
- Building a general-purpose authorization engine.
- Probabilistic entity resolution as a required core feature.
- Runtime answer generation, agent planning, or citation prose formatting.
- Backend-specific retrieval schemas or filter languages.

items.title: 把「模板定义」写进 CONTEXT.md 并补 ADR

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Maintainer needs to evaluate this issue

items.body:
## 背景

#88 引入了「模板定义」：租户对一个分析模板的参数，带版本，按映射的规则双人发布。这个概念现在只写在代码注释里（`app/.server/db/schema.ts` 的 `template_definitions` / `template_versions`、`app/.server/templates.ts` 的文件头），`CONTEXT.md` 里没有这个词，也没有 ADR。

`CONTEXT.md` 里「分析模板（Template）」（:177）写的是「成员填参数即得到一份指标或标签定义」，和现在的实现对不上：现在填参数得到的是一份模板定义，不是指标定义或标签定义。

## 要记下的决定

- 模板定义按租户、按模板各一份，第一次保存草稿时建立；没有已发布版本时用模板注册表里的默认参数。
- 双人发布的规则同 ADR-0015（发布者不能是最后保存草稿的人）。起草和丢弃需要 `definitions:draft`，所以分析师也能起草、丢弃；发布需要 `publish`。
- 定义里不含每次运行时给定的参数（如 RFM 的 `asOf`）。发布后以当天（UTC）为 `asOf` 入队一次模板任务，任务参数带 `definitionVersion`，快照登记时记下。
- 发布模板时只锁定义行，不像发布映射那样锁租户行。

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CONTEXT.md` 增加「模板定义」词条，并改正「分析模板」词条，和实现一致
- [ ] 新增一份 ADR 记录上面的决定（或补进 ADR-0004、0015），并在 `docs/adr/README.md` 的索引里加一行


## Implementation guide

纯文档改动，约 35–45 行。没有测试或 lint 读取 CONTEXT.md / docs/adr，不用改 test/README.md。

- **Change**: `CONTEXT.md:177` 「分析模板（Template）」（`### 定义与产出` 小节，:172）：把「成员填参数即得到一份指标或标签定义」改成「填参数得到一份模板定义」，并说明产出的是快照。
- **New**（词条）: `CONTEXT.md`，插在「分析模板」正文之后、:180「标签定义」之前：`**模板定义（Template Definition）**：` 段落。写清楚：按租户、按模板各一份，带版本，双人发布，不含运行参数（`asOf`），没有已发布版本时用注册表默认参数。末尾写「见 ADR-0021」。
- **Change**: `CONTEXT.md:189` 「发布」、`CONTEXT.md:193` 「草稿」：两处现在只列了映射和指标 / 标签定义，要把模板定义加进去，否则又和实现对不上。
- **New**: `docs/adr/0021-template-definitions.md`（文件名暂拟）。结构照 0019 / 0020：
  - `# 结论式中文标题`
  - 背景段落
  - 若干 `**小标题。** 正文` 段落
  - `## 已接受的取舍`
  - 引用 0004 和 0015
- **Change**: `docs/adr/README.md:27` 之后加一行 `| [0021](0021-….md) | 一句话决定 | 改到这些地方时要读 |`。可选：在 0004 那行的「改到这些地方时要读」里加上「模板定义」。
- **Reuse**（ADR 要写的事实及出处，都已核实）：
  - 表：`template_definitions` 在 `app/.server/db/schema.ts:306`，(tenant_id, template) 唯一。`template_versions` 在 :315，字段 params jsonb、authors[]、last_editor、published_by_email；部分唯一索引保证一个定义同时只有一份草稿（:331）。
  - 第一次保存草稿时建立定义行：`saveDraft` 在 `app/.server/templates.ts:72`，:77 用 `onConflictDoNothing`。
  - 回落默认参数：`getTemplate` 在 :45，:63 是 `published?.params ?? TEMPLATES[t].defaults`。注册表在 `app/.server/pipeline/templates/index.ts:17`。
  - 双人发布：`publishBlocker(actor, version)` 在 `app/.server/publish-rules.ts:13`，映射（`mappings.ts:225`）和模板（`templates.ts:116`）共用。
  - 权限：`app/.server/access.ts` 中 `definitions:draft` 在 :10，`publish` 在 :12，analyst 在 :29（有 draft、没有 publish）。路由 action 在 `app/routes/analytics.templates.$id.tsx:90`。
  - 发布后入队：`templates.ts:137` 取 UTC 当天作 `asOf`，:138 调 `insertTask(..., { ...definition, asOf, definitionVersion })`。handler 在 `pipeline/handlers.ts:192`，会先剥掉 `definitionVersion` 再解析参数。快照登记 `registerSnapshot` 在 `app/.server/snapshots.ts:40`，存进 `schema.ts:340` 的 `definition_version` 列。
  - 锁：模板发布只锁定义行（`templates.ts:121` `.for('update')`，:120 的注释说明了理由）；映射发布先锁租户行（`mappings.ts:230`），再锁映射行。
- **ADRs**: 0004、0015。建议新建 0021，不要补进那两份：0004 只讲不用 dbt，0015 讲的是映射和标准层合并。
- **Watch out**（票面没写、ADR 里应补上的事实）：
  - 映射的起草和丢弃要 `sources:write`（ADR-0015:13），模板定义复用的是 `definitions:draft`，所以分析师也能起草和丢弃。ADR 要写明这个差异。
  - 从没发布过的定义，丢弃草稿时整个定义行会被删掉（`templates.ts:162`），之后回到默认参数。
  - 直接给参数入队的任务不带 `definitionVersion`，这时快照的 `definition_version` 为空（`schema.ts:335` 的注释）。
- **Decide**:
  - 要不要顺手把 `access.ts:10` 的说明「起草指标与标签定义」改成包含模板定义（改 1 行代码文案）。
  - ADR 文件的 slug。

items.title: feat: multi-cloud provider extension — Azure + GCP alongside AWS + Cloudflare
items.body:
## Context

Issue #1 scoped the AWS (hashicorp/aws) and Cloudflare providers for managing existing resources (SES, Lightsail → EC2, R2 BSL).

This issue extends `versions.tf` with Azure (`azurerm`) and GCP (`google`) providers and adds the first resource sets for each, within the €10/month hard cap per provider.

## Governance rules

- Free tier mandatory first choice
- Billing alert at €8/provider before the €10 hard cap
- All resources in code — no console-only resources
- Monthly review check in minicloud-ops

## Scope

### `versions.tf` additions

```hcl
required_providers {
  # existing
  maas       = { source = "canonical/maas",     version = "~> 2.5" }
  aws        = { source = "hashicorp/aws",       version = "~> 5.0" }
  cloudflare = { source = "cloudflare/cloudflare", version = "~> 4.0" }
  # new
  azurerm    = { source = "hashicorp/azurerm",  version = "~> 3.0" }
  google     = { source = "hashicorp/google",   version = "~> 6.0" }
}
```

### `azure_provider.tf`

```hcl
provider "azurerm" {
  features {}
  subscription_id = var.azure_subscription_id
  client_id       = var.azure_client_id
  client_secret   = var.azure_client_secret
  tenant_id       = var.azure_tenant_id
}
```

### `azure_entra.tf` — Entra External Identities B2C tenant

- `azurerm_aadb2c_directory` resource — External Identities tenant (free ≤50k MAU)
- Variables: `azure_b2c_display_name`, `azure_b2c_domain_name`, `azure_resource_group`
- Output: `azure_b2c_tenant_id` (used by platform-backlog IAM-3 OIDC config)

### `gcp_provider.tf`

```hcl
provider "google" {
  project = var.gcp_project_id
  region  = var.gcp_region  # europe-west1 (Belgium, closest to SFR)
}
```

### `gcp_bigquery.tf` — Insurance analytics dataset

```hcl
resource "google_bigquery_dataset" "insurance_analytics" {
  dataset_id = "insurance_analytics"
  location   = "EU"
  description = "Daily exports from ClickHouse for ad-hoc analytics (GDP-3)"
}

resource "google_bigquery_table" "dim_employee" { ... }
resource "google_bigquery_table" "fact_headcount_monthly" { ... }
resource "google_bigquery_table" "fact_claims_monthly" { ... }
resource "google_bigquery_table" "fact_policy_monthly" { ... }
```

Schemas mirror the dbt mart schemas from ClickHouse (GDP-1 #152).

### `env.sh` additions

```bash
# Azure
export ARM_CLIENT_ID="..."
export ARM_CLIENT_SECRET="..."
export ARM_TENANT_ID="..."
export ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID="..."

# GCP
export GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS="$(cat ~/.gcp/minicloud-sa-key.json)"
export TF_VAR_gcp_project_id="minicloud-platform"
export TF_VAR_gcp_region="europe-west1"
```

### `variables.tf` additions

Azure + GCP variable blocks with descriptions and no defaults (secrets must be provided via env).

## Dependencies

- platform-backlog IAM-3 (Azure Entra External Identities) — consumes `azure_b2c_tenant_id` output
- platform-backlog GDP-3 (GCP BigQuery) — consumes dataset IDs

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `tofu init` succeeds with all 5 providers
- [ ] `tofu plan` shows Azure B2C tenant + GCP BigQuery dataset (no apply needed until accounts created)
- [ ] `env.sh.example` updated with all new variables (no real secrets)
- [ ] `README.md` updated with provider setup instructions
- [ ] Neither provider resource incurs cost (free tier only at this stage)

items.title: architecture: Map implemented components to canonical authority

labels.name: priority: medium
labels.description: Medium priority - important but not blocking

items.body:
## Problem
`pnpm planning:db:integrity:check` currently reports 54 `component_missing_architecture_authority` warnings. The affected components are implemented, but their Planning DB records are `unplanned` and have no canonical architecture authority relation. The source view identifies the generated index path as:

```text
.generated-docs/planning/status/system-governance-component-index.components.yaml
```

This is an authority mapping gap, not proof that the corresponding code does not exist. Each component needs an explicit link to an accepted design identity, ADR, governed component document, or other Planning DB-backed architecture evidence. Inventory commands:

```text
pnpm planning:db:query component-integrity --limit 500
pnpm planning:db:query component-roadmap --limit 500
```

The warning passes only because the progressive baseline allows 54 findings. That baseline must not substitute for architecture ownership.

## Governing sources

- `AGENTS.md`
- `docs/planning/status/governance-document-rule-inventory.md`
- `docs/architecture/command-query-rail-governance.md`
- `docs/architecture/components/ci-governance/component-engineering-record-component.md`
- `ADR-0061` (Planning DB owns components, relations, ownership, and architecture evidence)
- Planning DB `architecture-designs` authority query

## Proposed solution

Build a canonical component-to-architecture-authority reconciliation:

1. Export all 54 affected component IDs and names.
2. Match each component to an existing Planning DB architecture design, accepted ADR, canonical component document, or governed evidence path.
3. Reuse existing authority identities; do not create synonyms or a second architecture catalog.
4. For components with no legitimate architecture authority, classify them explicitly as grouping/operational metadata and define the supported authority posture, or retire/reclassify them through the existing Planning DB mechanism.
5. Make the generated component index consume the canonical relation rather than infer authority from filesystem presence.
6. Add an integrity test preventing an implemented component from remaining `unplanned` without an explicit approved exception.
7. Reduce the progressive baseline from 54 to the residual count and then remove the residual through follow-up work.

## Acceptance criteria

- `pnpm planning:db:query component-integrity --limit 500` reports no unexpected `component_missing_architecture_authority` rows.
- Every affected component has exactly one canonical authority posture: linked design/ADR/evidence, explicitly valid grouping component, or governed retirement/reclassification.
- No duplicate architecture authority, local task tracker, or parallel document index is introduced.
- The generated component index and Planning DB query agree on authority state.
- `pnpm planning:db:integrity:check --strict` passes without a progressive-baseline regression.
- Validation evidence and residual exceptions are recorded in this issue and the implementation PR.

## Out of scope

- Replacing Planning DB with generated Markdown.
- Creating one new ADR per component without a durable decision.
- Treating issue status as architecture authority.
- Suppressing the warning or increasing the baseline.

items.title: feat: scaffold a new dbt project in a folder, linked to a given Fabric DW (dbt-fabric)
items.body:
## Summary

Add a command that scaffolds a **new dbt project** in a given folder, pre-wired to a given Fabric Data Warehouse via the `dbt-fabric` adapter. The CLI already resolves the warehouse's SQL endpoint host + name + auth mode, so it can generate a ready-to-run `profiles.yml` / `dbt_project.yml` without the user hand-editing connection details.

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/data-warehouse/tutorial-setup-dbt

## What "linked to the given Fabric DW" means

`dbt-fabric` profile (verified from the Fabric tutorial):
```yaml
config:
  partial_parse: true
<project_name>:
  target: dev
  outputs:
    dev:
      type: fabric
      driver: ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server
      host: <SQL analytics endpoint>     # ← warehouse.connection_string
      database: <warehouse name>          # ← warehouse.display_name
      schema: dbo
      threads: 4
      authentication: CLI                 # CLI (interactive) | ServicePrincipal (automation) | auto
```
We populate `host` from the resolved warehouse connection string, `database` from the warehouse name, and `authentication` from the CLI's auth mode. **SQL auth is not supported by dbt-fabric — Entra only.**

## Files to scaffold (in the given folder)
- `dbt_project.yml` — project name, `profile:`, model paths, version.
- `profiles.yml` — project-local, with the `fabric` output above (note: dbt reads CWD then `~/.dbt`; document running dbt from the folder or `DBT_PROFILES_DIR`). Option to instead merge into `~/.dbt/profiles.yml` (back up existing).
- `models/` with a tiny example staging model + `models/staging/_sources.yml`. Optionally **generate `_sources.yml` from the DW's actual schemas/tables** (reuse the schemas + tables list services) behind `--with-sources`.
- `.gitignore` (`target/`, `dbt_packages/`, `logs/`, `.user.yml`).
- `README.md` — prerequisites + next steps (`pip install dbt-fabric`, ODBC Driver 18, `dbt debug`, `dbt run`).

## Proposed surface

### CLI — `fabric-dw dbt init <ws> <item> <folder>`
- `--project-name NAME` (default: sanitized folder name; must be valid dbt project id — lowercase snake_case, no leading digit).
- `--profile-name NAME` (default: project name).
- `--schema dbo`, `--target dev`, `--threads 4`.
- `--auth auto|cli|sp|interactive` (default: mirror the CLI's current auth mode). Mapping: `default→auto` (DefaultAzureCredential), `interactive→CLI`/`ActiveDirectoryInteractive`, `sp→ServicePrincipal`.
- `--profiles-dir project|home` (default `project`).
- `--with-sources` — generate `_sources.yml` from the DW schemas/tables.
- `--force` — allow scaffolding into a non-empty folder.

### Service/helper — `src/fabric_dw/services/dbt_scaffold.py` (or CLI-local)
- Builds file contents from the resolved warehouse (`host = connection_string`, `database = display_name`). Reuse `build_sql_target` / warehouse resolution. Use template files via `importlib.resources` (no new heavy deps).

### MCP (optional / minimal)
- A `generate_dbt_profile(workspace, item, ...)` tool that **returns** the `profiles.yml` / `dbt_project.yml` content as text (the MCP server can't write to the user's local folder). Local scaffolding is CLI-first.

## Implementation notes
- **Never write secrets**: for `ServicePrincipal`, emit `tenant_id`/`client_id`/`client_secret` as `"{{ env_var('AZURE_...') }}"` placeholders, not literals. Default to `auto`/`CLI` (no secrets needed).
- **Auth mapping** mirrors the CLI's `CredentialMode`.
- **Folder safety**: create the folder if missing; refuse a non-empty folder unless `--force`; when merging into `~/.dbt/profiles.yml`, back up the existing file and merge (don't clobber other profiles).
- **Project name validation**: sanitize/validate to a legal dbt identifier.
- **Prerequisites are the user's**: we scaffold files only. Note that running dbt needs `pip install dbt-fabric` + ODBC Driver 18 (separate from this CLI's `mssql-python`). Optionally run a best-effort `dbt debug` if `dbt` is on `PATH` (don't hard-require it).
- Docs: add a `dbt` section to `docs/cli.md`.
- Tests: unit tests assert generated `profiles.yml`/`dbt_project.yml` contents for a resolved warehouse (host/database/auth mapping), project-name sanitization, non-empty-folder refusal, and `--with-sources` generation (mocked schemas/tables); a smoke test that the scaffold is valid YAML.

## Out of scope (possible follow-ups)
- Running `dbt run`/`seed`/`test` or managing a dbt virtualenv/install.
- Non-Fabric adapters (synapse/etc.).
- Full opinionated project layout (marts/staging/intermediate conventions) beyond a minimal working scaffold.
- Generating models from existing tables (could pair with `--with-sources`).

## References
- Set up dbt for Fabric DW: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/data-warehouse/tutorial-setup-dbt
- dbt-fabric adapter setup: https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/core/connect-data-platform/fabric-setup
- dbt-fabric configs: https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/resource-configs/fabric-configs
- Roadmap #71

items.title: docs: feature guide — set up a dbt environment (new warehouse + dbt project)
items.body:
## Summary

Add a **feature guide** to the docs site that walks an analytics engineer end-to-end through standing up a dbt working environment on Microsoft Fabric: **provision a new Warehouse → obtain its SQL connection details → scaffold/connect a dbt project → verify the connection**.

Unlike the (closed) generic Getting Started walkthrough (#70, CLI + MCP from Claude), this guide is scoped to the dbt workflow and ties together features that already exist in the project — it is documentation only; no new code is required.

> **Reconcile with the shipped `dbt-setup` Agent Skill.** A user-invocable Agent Skill, `dbt-setup` (`skills/dbt-setup/SKILL.md`, documented at `docs/skills.md`), already automates this exact scaffold via the MCP tools (`get_warehouse` → `list_schemas`/`list_tables` → `generate_dbt_profile` → write files → `dbt debug`/`dbt run`). This proposed guide overlaps heavily with it, and that overlap is intentional and worth calling out explicitly in the page: **the guide is the human, copy-pasteable narrative for someone driving `fabric-dw` from a terminal; the skill is the AI-assistant automation** that performs the same steps from an MCP client (Claude). The guide must cross-link the skill ("If you use an AI assistant, the `dbt-setup` skill does all of this for you") and the skill page should link back to the guide. Do not duplicate the skill's step list verbatim — frame the guide around the CLI commands and describe the skill as the assistant-driven equivalent.

## Purpose & target audience

- **Audience:** analytics engineers / data engineers starting a new dbt project against a Fabric Data Warehouse who want a repeatable, scriptable setup instead of clicking through the Fabric portal.
- **Goal:** from "I have a workspace and capacity" to "`dbt debug` passes and `dbt run` builds a model" using `fdw` to do the provisioning and to generate a correct `profiles.yml` automatically — no manual copy/paste of the SQL endpoint or hand-writing YAML.
- **Why it matters:** Microsoft's own tutorial requires the reader to manually find the SQL analytics endpoint in the portal and hand-author `profiles.yml`. `fabric-dw` already automates exactly that (`dbt init` / `generate_dbt_profile`), so a guide closes the gap between Microsoft's manual steps and our automated path.

## CLI / MCP features to tie together (all already implemented)

End-to-end workflow: **provision → get connection → configure dbt profile → verify**. Every reference below is grounded in the current source (verified 2026-06-20).

> **Workspace is a global option, not a positional argument.** None of the commands below take a positional `WORKSPACE`. The target workspace comes from the global `-w/--workspace NAME|GUID` option (or the configured default set with `fdw config set workspace <name|id>`). Examples below show `fdw -w "<workspace>" <command>`.

### 1. Authenticate

- Global `--auth {default|sp|interactive}` (default: `default`); credential chain in `src/fabric_dw/auth.py` (`CredentialMode`, `DefaultAzureCredential`, `ClientSecretCredential`, interactive browser, GitHub Actions OIDC). Scopes: `FABRIC_SCOPE` (`https://analysis.windows.net/powerbi/api/.default`, control plane), `SQL_SCOPE` (`https://database.windows.net/.default`, TDS).
  - **Note:** there is **no `FABRIC_AUTH` environment variable** — auth mode is selected only via the `--auth` flag. Relevant env vars are `AZURE_TENANT_ID` / `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` / `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` (for `sp`), and optionally `FABRIC_INTERACTIVE_CLIENT_ID` / `FABRIC_INTERACTIVE_TENANT_ID` (for `interactive`). Link to the Authentication reference (`docs/authentication.md`) for the canonical list.
- This same mode is what the scaffolder maps into the dbt profile (see step 4).

### 2. Provision the warehouse

- CLI: `fdw warehouses create NAME [--collation] [--description]` (`src/fabric_dw/cli/commands/warehouses.py`). `NAME` is positional; the workspace is the global `-w` option.
- Service: `warehouses.create()` (`src/fabric_dw/services/warehouses.py`) issues `POST /workspaces/{ws}/warehouses`, then **polls the create LRO to completion** and re-`GET`s the warehouse so the returned object is fully populated (handles both the 202+`Location` LRO path and the synchronous 201 path, plus transient empty-2xx retries — issue #204).
- MCP equivalent: `create_warehouse` (`src/fabric_dw/mcp/tools/warehouses.py`).
- Optional: `fdw warehouses takeover` (set ownership) and `fdw warehouses permissions` — relevant when a service principal/team needs access; `permissions` listing requires Fabric Administrator.

### 3. Get the SQL connection details dbt needs

dbt's `profiles.yml` needs `host` (server) and `database`. In Fabric these are:

- **`host`** = the **SQL analytics endpoint connection string** (the TDS server, `<guid>.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com`). Surfaced by:
  - `fdw sql-endpoints get [ITEM]` and `fdw sql-endpoints list` (`src/fabric_dw/cli/commands/sql_endpoints.py`). (`ITEM` is the endpoint name/GUID; workspace is the global `-w` option. The group also has `refresh` and `permissions`.)
  - Service `sql_endpoints.get_endpoint_connection_string()` (`src/fabric_dw/services/sql_endpoints.py`) **polls until the connection string is non-empty** (default timeout 120 s) — important because the endpoint is provisioned with eventual consistency right after `warehouses create`. For lakehouse-derived endpoints, the value is read from the parent Lakehouse's `sqlEndpointProperties.connectionString`.
  - Internally the scaffolder reuses `build_sql_target()` (`src/fabric_dw/cli/commands/_utils.py`) which reads `entry.connection_string` from the resolver/cache, so `dbt init` does **not** require a manual `sql-endpoints get` step — it resolves the host itself.
- **`database`** = the **warehouse display name** (Fabric uses the item name as the Initial Catalog / database). The scaffolder uses `target_obj.database` = the resolved item display name.

### 4. Configure the dbt profile (the feature that does it all)

- CLI: `fdw dbt init [ITEM] FOLDER` (`src/fabric_dw/cli/commands/dbt.py`). `ITEM` (warehouse name/GUID, optional — falls back to the configured default) is positional, `FOLDER` is the target directory; workspace is the global `-w` option. Scaffolds `dbt_project.yml`, `profiles.yml`, `requirements.txt` (`dbt-core`, `dbt-fabric`), `.gitignore`, standard dirs (`models`, `analyses`, `macros`, `seeds`, `snapshots`, `tests`, each with `.gitkeep`), a sample model (`models/my_first_model.sql`), `models/staging/_sources.yml`, a `README.md`, and (with `--with-sources`) a real `models/staging/_sources.yml` introspected from the live warehouse's schemas/tables/columns. Runs `git init` when git is on PATH and the folder has no `.git`.
  - Options to document (verified against `fdw dbt init --help`):
    - `--project-name` — dbt project name (default: sanitized folder name).
    - `--profile-name` — dbt profile name (default: same as project name).
    - `--schema` — default target schema (default `dbo`).
    - `--target` — dbt target name (default `dev`).
    - `--threads` — number of dbt threads, `IntRange(1, 64)` (default `4`).
    - `--auth {auto|CLI|ServicePrincipal|interactive|sp}` — dbt-fabric authentication override. Defaults to the CLI's current `--auth` mode (`default→auto`, `interactive→CLI`, `sp→ServicePrincipal`). `interactive` and `sp` are accepted aliases for `CLI` and `ServicePrincipal`.
    - `--profiles-dir {project|home}` (default `project`) — `project` writes `profiles.yml` in the project folder; `home` merges into `~/.dbt/profiles.yml` (backs up an existing file).
    - `--with-sources` — generate `models/staging/_sources.yml` from the warehouse's actual schemas, tables, and column data types.
    - `--force` — scaffold into a non-empty folder instead of refusing.
- MCP: `generate_dbt_profile` tool (`src/fabric_dw/mcp/tools/dbt.py`) returns the same file contents **as strings** (the MCP server can't write the caller's filesystem). It returns a dict with keys `profiles_yml`, `dbt_project_yml`, `sources_yml`, `requirements_txt`, `gitignore`. Document this as the AI-assistant path (and note the `dbt-setup` skill orchestrates it end-to-end).
- Scaffolder internals worth surfacing in the guide (`src/fabric_dw/services/dbt_scaffold.py`):
  - Generated `profiles.yml` is `type: fabric`, `driver: ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server`, `host` = connection string, `database` = warehouse name, `authentication` = mapped mode, plus a top-level `config: {partial_parse: true}` block and a `target`/`outputs` structure.
  - **Auth mapping** `auth_mode_to_dbt()`: CLI `default` → dbt `auto`, `interactive` → dbt `CLI`, `sp` → dbt `ServicePrincipal`.
  - **Security:** for `ServicePrincipal`, secrets are emitted as `{{ env_var('AZURE_TENANT_ID') }}` / `{{ env_var('AZURE_CLIENT_ID') }}` / `{{ env_var('AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET') }}` placeholders — never literal secrets.

### 5. Verify

- Run `pip install -r requirements.txt` (in a separate env), then `dbt debug` and `dbt run` (per the generated `README.md`).
- Optionally cross-check from `fabric-dw` itself: `fdw sql exec [ITEM] -q "select 1"` (the `sql` group was restructured — it is now `fdw sql exec` / `fdw sql plan`, **not** `fdw sql query`) and `fdw tables list [ITEM]` to confirm the model materialized.

### How the CLI feeds dbt's profiles.yml (mapping table for the guide)

| dbt `profiles.yml` key | Fabric value | How `fabric-dw` supplies it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `fabric` | hard-coded by scaffolder |
| `driver` | `ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server` | hard-coded by scaffolder |
| `host` | SQL analytics endpoint (TDS server) | `sql-endpoints get` / resolved `connection_string`, polled until ready |
| `database` | warehouse display name (Initial Catalog) | resolved item name |
| `schema` | `dbo` (default) | `--schema` |
| `threads` | `4` (default) | `--threads` |
| `authentication` | `auto` / `CLI` / `ServicePrincipal` | mapped from `--auth` (`default→auto`, `interactive→CLI`, `sp→ServicePrincipal`) |

For `authentication: ServicePrincipal`, the profile also emits `tenant_id` / `client_id` / `client_secret` as `{{ env_var(...) }}` placeholders.

## Microsoft Learn recommendations to incorporate (with source URLs)

- **Set up dbt for Fabric Data Warehouse** (the canonical tutorial; profiles.yml shape, `host` = SQL analytics endpoint, `database` = warehouse name, `dbt debug/seed/run/test`): https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-warehouse/tutorial-setup-dbt
- **Prerequisites** — Python, **Microsoft ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server**, `pip install dbt-fabric`, create a warehouse: https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-warehouse/tutorial-setup-dbt#prerequisites-for-the-dbt-adapter-for-microsoft-fabric
- **Authentication guidance** — *"recommended mode to interactively work on a warehouse is CLI; use service principals for automation"*; Entra ID for users/identities/SPs: https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-warehouse/tutorial-setup-dbt#considerations
- **Connect to Fabric Data Warehouse → Connect using dbt** — `dbt-fabric` uses `pyodbc` over TDS; **SQL authentication is NOT supported for dbt-fabric** (Entra-only): https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-warehouse/how-to-connect#connect-using-dbt
- **Find the warehouse connection string** — confirms `host` = SQL connection string (server) and the warehouse item name is the **Initial Catalog / database**: https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-warehouse/how-to-connect
- **Warehouse connectivity** — TDS on TCP 1433; SQL connection string semantics; security model: https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-warehouse/connectivity
- **Warehouse connectivity → Considerations and limitations** — SQL auth unsupported; **remove `MultipleActiveResultSets`**; `InitialCatalog` / `master` behavior; transient connection errors & retry: https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-warehouse/connectivity#considerations-and-limitations
- **Microsoft Entra authentication as an alternative to SQL authentication** — Entra modes (Interactive / Service Principal / Password); sample server name `<guid>.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com`: https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-warehouse/entra-id-authentication
- **Create a warehouse** (portal/REST context for what `warehouses create` automates): https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-warehouse/create-warehouse
- **Fabric Data Warehouse limitations** & **T-SQL surface area** (link from the Limitations section): https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-warehouse/limitations and https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-warehouse/tsql-surface-area
- **(Secondary, non-MS Learn)** dbt-fabric adapter setup & resource configs (for SP fields in profiles.yml): https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/core/connect-data-platform/fabric-setup and https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/resource-configs/fabric-configs

> Note / gap: Microsoft's tutorial assumes you create the warehouse and find the SQL endpoint **in the portal**. This guide's value-add is showing the fully scriptable `fabric-dw` path. There is no MS Learn page documenting `fabric-dw` itself (it's a community tool), so the provisioning/scaffolding steps are grounded in this repo's source, while the dbt-side configuration and limitations are grounded in MS Learn above.
